articles.title_orig: China urges France, Germany to uphold open cooperation, free trade
articles.title_zh: China urges France, Germany to uphold open cooperation, free trade
articles.content_orig:
BEIJING – China hopes that France and Germany will uphold open cooperation and free trade, observe World Trade Organization rules and refrain from encouraging the European Union to use protectionist tools at every turn, the Ministry of Commerce said on Tuesday.
When asked to comment on media reports that France and Germany had urged the EU to make greater use of trade defense measures and roll out a number of new protectionist tools, a spokesperson for the ministry said China has always maintained that interdependence is not a risk, intertwined interests do not pose a threat, and open cooperation represents the right path to development.
READ MORE: Wang urges China, Germany to boost cooperation, uphold free trade
Protectionism cannot enhance competitiveness, and decoupling and cutting off supply chains will only harm others without benefiting oneself, the spokesperson said.
As major economies, France and Germany should not politicize trade and economic issues or overstretch the concept of national security. They should avoid going down the wrong path in the wrong way, which would ultimately backfire on themselves, the spokesperson added.

articles.title_orig: US military will execute Fort Hood shooter by firing squad, a first in 60 years
articles.title_zh: US military will execute Fort Hood shooter by firing squad, a first in 60 years
articles.content_orig:
An undated handout image of Hasan that was released by authorities in 2012
The Pentagon has announced it will execute a former US Army major by firing squad, the first military execution in more than 60 years.
Nidal Hasan fatally shot 13 unarmed US soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009, injuring another 32.
Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell announced on social media on Monday that US defence secretary Pete Hegseth had made the recommendation and President Donald Trump approved it.
The execution is scheduled to take place at Fort Hood in Texas on 3 December, the secretary of the US Army said on Tuesday. It will be the first military execution by firing squad since the end of World War Two.
"Judgement day for Hasan has finally come," Parnell wrote on X.
Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist from Virginia, killed 13 soldiers at the base in Texas in 2009 and later admitted in court he was the gunman and apologised for "any mistakes".
He said during his court-martial in 2013 that he believed he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan.
The killings on 5 November 2009 were the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American military base.
The attack took place in a crowded medical building where deploying soldiers were awaiting check-ups and vaccines.
Watch: Why is America running out of execution drugs? , external
Hasan is currently one of four inmates on the US military's death row.
A military execution requires approval from the US president, according to military law.
It also requires appellate review and a final judgment on its legality to move forward.
The US Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces deemed the military death penalty unconstitutional in 1983 but it was reinstated the following year by an executive order under then-President Ronald Reagan.
Military executions differ from those carried out at the state level.
The majority of executions in the US are carried out on the state level, with 27 states, the military and the federal government still having capital punishment as a legally available option.
Death by firing squad is rather uncommon. There was an execution by firing squad carried out last year in South Carolina, a first for the state and the first time the method was used in the US in 15 years.
Four other states allow the use of a firing squad, including Idaho, Mississippi, Oklahoma and Utah.
How widely used is the death penalty in the US?
Trump has been a proponent of the federal death penalty and re-instated it through an executive order on the first day of his administration in January 2025.
Under his predecessor, former President Joe Biden, the justice department had issued a moratorium on the federal use of the death penalty.
The executive order signed by Trump describes capital punishment as "an essential tool for deterring and punishing those who would commit the most heinous crimes and acts of lethal violence against American citizens".

articles.title_orig: Obama-era DOJ official to lead review of Cornell response to rape allegations
articles.title_zh: Obama-era DOJ official to lead review of Cornell response to rape allegations
articles.content_orig:
Cornell University trustees have named former United States Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates to conduct an independent internal review of how the university handles allegations of sexual assault and harassment, following widespread criticism over its response to a former student’s rape allegations.
The trustees announced on Tuesday that Yates will examine how Cornell investigates reports of sexual misconduct and assault, its disciplinary procedures, campus police responses and the university’s oversight of fraternities.
Yates served as deputy attorney general during the administration of former President Barack Obama and as acting attorney general at the start of Donald Trump’s first presidency. Trump fired her in 2017 after she directed Justice Department lawyers not to defend his initial travel ban that targeted Muslim-majority countries.
“It is imperative that Cornell be willing to examine itself with the same rigor we expect of others,” Cornell Board of Trustees Chair Anne Meinig Smalling said in a statement.
The appointment comes after renewed criticism of Cornell’s handling of allegations made by a woman, identified in court filings as Jane Doe , who said she was sexually assaulted by multiple members of the Chi Phi fraternity in October 2024.
The case resurfaced after Doe filed a civil lawsuit against the university, the fraternity and seven former students in September.
No criminal charges have been filed in the case. Cornell has said it expelled some students and suspended others who were accused following its own investigation, while the Chi Phi chapter was shut down.
“We don’t have all the answers, but we are committed to investigating and finding the answers our community deserves,” Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff said in a video message on Saturday.
Yates, now a partner at the law firm King & Spalding, conducts independent investigations and previously led a 2022 investigation into sexual abuse and misconduct in the National Women’s Soccer League that found systemic failures.
New York Attorney General Letitia James is separately conducting a criminal investigation into the allegations after Governor Kathy Hochul appointed her special prosecutor last week.
Hochul had called for an independent review of Cornell’s handling of the case amid criticism from students, faculty and others.

articles.title_orig: Chinese woman snaps up nearly 200 parking spots to flip to neighbours for profit
articles.title_zh: Chinese woman snaps up nearly 200 parking spots to flip to neighbours for profit
articles.content_orig:
Residents argue that parking is a vital community asset that should not be monopolised by anyone seeking financial gain from resale
A woman in central China invested 14 million yuan (US$2 million) to acquire 196 parking spaces in a residential community, later selling them at a significant mark-up, which led to furious residents suing her.
The lawsuit centred around a residential block, the name of which was not disclosed, located in Changsha, Hunan province.
The property project was completed and put on the market in 2018. At the time, many were sceptical about the community’s prospects due to a lack of essential public facilities such as shops, schools, and public transport options. Consequently, there was little interest in both the flats and the parking spaces, according to Hunan TV.
Despite this pessimism, a woman surnamed Wu snapped up 196 parking spots in a single transaction, representing 40 per cent of the project’s total parking inventory, for a sum of 14 million yuan. The developer, facing severe cash constraints, agreed to her purchase.

articles.title_orig: Trump worries Iran could target U.S. cities. These places get extra nuclear protection
articles.title_zh: Trump worries Iran could target U.S. cities. These places get extra nuclear protection
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
President Donald Trump has sparked outrage after appearing to suggest Iran “take out” two American cities.
Speaking at a rally in Grand Island, Nebraska , Monday, the commander-in-chief addressed the subject of high gas prices sparked by Operation Epic Fury.
“Remember, with the war, it’s just artificial,” Trump said of the soaring costs. “It’s a little bit high.” The national average fuel price stands at $4.37 a gallon as of Tuesday morning, according to the AAA.
“It’s a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe,” he continued, before adding: “They can take out a city – let ’em take, let ’em take out Los Angeles, let ’em take out San Diego. That’s – this is a very small price to pay.”
“And it’s going to be over very soon,” Trump continued. “It’s essentially almost over with. And they might keep going a little long, you know. They always say they have a big threshold for pain. They need it, let me tell you.”
While Trump’s remarks on the Democrat-run cities drew cheers from the MAGA crowd in Nebraska, there was swift backlash from Golden State lawmakers.
California Gov. Gavin Newsom wrote in a post on X : “After sending the National Guard and Marines to occupy California, Donald Trump is now saying our foreign enemies should ‘take out’ Los Angeles and San Diego. He is deranged and dangerous.”
“The role of a president is to protect the country, not to actively threaten it and encourage attacks on American lives,” added L.A. Mayor Karen Bass in a post of her own.
Her San Diego counterpart, Mayor Todd Gloria, was equally indignant : “San Diego is not collateral damage. We are not expendable. And we are never a ‘small price to pay.’ Keep our city out of your reckless war talk.”
San Diego city councilmember and Democratic congressional candidate Marni von Wilpert suggested Trump’s remark provided grounds for an unprecedented third impeachment.
“This is an impeachable offense by the commander-in-chief, who swore an oath to protect our country,” she said . “Our homes, our families and our communities cannot be treated as collateral damage or a political punchline by this president.”
Even the Trump-backed San Diego County Supervisor Jim Desmond, a Republican and Navy veteran running against Von Wilpert, said he “vehemently” disagreed with the president.
“Our job is to keep Americans safe, stand up to our enemies, and make sure a threat like that never becomes reality,” he posted . “No American city is expendable, and no American family should ever be treated as collateral damage.”
The latest estimated cost of the Iran war that Trump started alongside Israel’s Benjamin Netanyahu earlier this year is $43 billion, according to the Department of Defense.
So far 19 U.S. soldiers have been killed in the Persian Gulf so far since the conflict began on February 28, with hundreds more wounded .

articles.title_orig: Ukraine Drone Attack Sets Fire On Oil Tanker With 23 Indian Crew Members
articles.title_zh: Ukraine Drone Attack Sets Fire On Oil Tanker With 23 Indian Crew Members
articles.content_orig:
Two injured crew members from one of the ships have been sent for treatment
A civilian cargo ship has sunk and its crew is missing after being attacked by drones in the Black Sea, Bulgarian officials say.
A second vessel - carrying grain - was also hit within Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said. Its 18 crew were rescued.
Radev did not say who was behind the attacks, which come as Russia intensifies strikes in the Black Sea, particularly the eastern side, as part of its war against Ukraine.
Moscow has not commented on the latest incident, a day after it was accused by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky of striking a civilian vessel carrying corn. EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the attacks were "unacceptable".
Air and sea drones were involved in the attacks at about 03:00 (23:00 GMT), some 70 miles (112 km) off the coastal town of Byala in eastern Bulgaria, Radev said.
The sunken ship was flying under the flag of Togo, he said. Named the Alfa Watan, it was a Turkish-owned general cargo ship and was reportedly heading for Sulina, Romania.
It is not clear what the Alfa Watan was carrying or how many people were on board.
A Bulgarian vessel was close by, but when they arrived all they saw was an overturned boat and rafts as well as life jackets. A search operation has been launched.
Radev said Bulgarian sailors had rescued the crew members from the second ship - including two who were injured in a fire on board. Eleven were Turkish and seven Indian nationals. That ship, the Able, was flying the flag of Palau and transporting grain.
Its last reported position was five nautical miles (9km) from the Alfa Watan.
Radev condemned the strikes as "a flagrant violation of maritime law".
He told reporters: "Such an attack within the Bulgarian exclusive economic zone is absolutely unacceptable."
He did not accuse Russia of carrying out the strikes, but referred to the war in Ukraine, saying: "As I have long maintained, if this war is not halted in time, it will continue to expand its geographical reach and increase risks, including the risk of a global conflict."
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wrote on X: "The situation in the Black Sea is increasingly concerning.
"Commercial ships â and innocent crews â are being targeted, with lives already lost at sea," she said. "While exact circumstances of these incidents are still being established, the developments are very concerning."
"Attacks on civilian shipping are unacceptable."
Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea is just over 29,000 sq km (11,197 sq miles), about 6% of the total size of the Black Sea.
A separate attack on Tuesday, near Odesa, saw a crew member killed and seven more injured. The ship was flying the flag of the Marshall Islands, according to Ukrainian media.
On Sunday, Russia's defence ministry said it would intensify its strikes across Ukraine in response to comments made by Zelensky earlier last week, in which he said Kyiv would ramp up its attacks on Russian oil refineries.
Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

articles.title_orig: Maine Senate Race Live Updates: Susan Collins and Troy Jackson Face Off in Midterms Debate
articles.title_zh: Maine Senate Race Live Updates: Susan Collins and Troy Jackson Face Off in Midterms Debate
articles.content_orig:
Republican challenged by Democrat Troy Jackson in critical Senate race says she opposes Iran war and Canada tariffs
Susan Collins, the Republican senator for Maine , pointedly distanced herself from Donald Trump in a televised debate with Democratic challenger Troy Jackson on Tuesday, as she sought to present an image of independence in a state that has voted against Trump three times.
Proclaiming herself as not the US president’s “favorite senator”, Collins made the highly unusual boast for a Republican that she had voted with Joe Biden, a Democrat, more than 90% of the time when he was president. She also emphasized her differences with her fellow Republicans , saying she voted against her own party more than any other senator.
Collins’ defensiveness came amid a determined onslaught from Jackson, 58, a veteran former state legislator who was getting his first chance to present himself to a broad audience since replacing Graham Platner as the Democratic candidate in a contest that could be vital to the party’s hopes of winning the Senate.
Platner, a former harbor master, was forced to withdraw from the race in July after facing sexual assault allegations, which he denied, leaving Democrats racing against the clock to replace a candidate who had built up momentum campaigning on a populist progressive platform.
Jackson painted Collins as a Trump loyalist, saying she voted with the president 96% of the time. He also doggedly focused on her 2018 vote for the conservative supreme court justice Brett Kavanaugh, tying it to the court’s subsequent overturning of Roe v Wade, which had for half a century guaranteed the national right to abortion.
“Tonight is about who you stand with when it matters,” Jackson said in a pithy opening statement. “Eight years ago today, Maine women went to DC and begged Senator Collins not to confirm Brett Kavanaugh, but she did it anyways.
“He helped overturn Roe v Wade, and today she says she has no regrets. Would you trust her to pick the next supreme court justice?”
Collins, 73, who has been a senator since 1996, has frequently presented herself as a moderate who stands against more radical trends in her own party. The posture is in line with Maine’s profile as a more Democratic-leaning state, which Trump has not won in any of his three presidential campaigns and which has voted for Democrat presidential candidates in every election since 1992.
Nevertheless, Collins went to unusual lengths to differentiate herself from Trump on a range of issues, including the war with Iran, which she said she voted to end nine times, calling it “not well thought out”.
Collins reacted with something close to alarm when the moderator, Gregg Lagerquist, said Trump had suggested that the president might pay a campaign visit to Maine.
“I don’t think that President Trump is going to come to Maine,” she said. “He’s talking about going to a lot of different states. I’ve heard nothing from his office, and I’m not exactly his favorite senator.”
Collins stressed her differences with the president on specific issues pertinent to the Maine economy, including rural healthcare and tariffs against Canada, with which the state shares a border.
“I have been the most outspoken opponent of the tariffs on Canada,” she said. “Canada is not China. It’s our neighbor and our friends.”
Polls show the two candidates running neck and neck.

articles.title_orig: Couple Charged With Conspiring to Abuse Numerous Surrogate Children
articles.title_zh: Couple Charged With Conspiring to Abuse Numerous Surrogate Children
articles.content_orig:
A California couple at the center of a surrogacy scandal was arrested on Tuesday. A law enforcement source confirmed the arrests to CBS News shortly before officials held a news conference to announce the latest developments.
Guojun Xuan and Silvia Zhang are being charged with multiple counts, including conspiracy to commit child abuse and dissuading a witness, Los Angeles District Attorney Nathan J. Hochman said.
The couple drew national headlines last year after authorities raided their Arcadia mansion in July 2025 and took 21 kids, mostly surrogate-born , into state custody.
Tuesday morning, detectives from the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department arrested the couple at their residence. They were then transferred to the Pasadena courthouse to be arraigned, Sheriff Robert Luna said. They both pleaded not guilty and are each being held on a $20 million bond.
A neighbor said Tuesday that helicopters and police could be seen at the couple's mansion and the entire block is taped off.
"What has been publicly filed in the complaint today is incredibly disturbing. It involves horrific punishment and beatings and child abuse," Hochman said at the news conference.
Officials said the investigation began in May 2025 when Zhang brought a 2-month-old boy to the hospital with a head injury.
"She appeared to be untruthful with hospital staff about how the injury was sustained and the hospital staff notified law enforcement authorities," Luna said, adding that when Arcadia police went to the home, "what they discovered raised even more serious concerns."
The district attorney said Tuesday that the children were seated for hours a day in three different rooms called "Learning Centers" under the supervision of various nannies at the couple's home, which he called a "house of horrors." The couple kept a system of 32 motion-activated cameras in the various rooms in the Arcadia mansion, he said. Footage from these cameras went to a television near their desk that the couple used to monitor the discipline given by the nannies.
Hochman said the nannies were caught on video spanking, slapping or hitting the children. One nanny, Chunmei Li,  allegedly struck the 2-month-old baby in the head, the district attorney said. A $105,000 warrant for her arrest was previously issued, but she remains on the run, he said.
Xuan's attorney, Mitchell Krems, said: "My client is innocent. It is the nanny's wrongdoing who went on the run. He is being targeted for exercising his constitutional right to have a large family."
Melissa Brisman, an attorney for two of the surrogates involved in the case, told CBS News, "This is wonderful news that people will be held responsible for their actions and there will be consequences if you abuse the surrogacy system."
Brisman added that it's important surrogacy remains an option for those who need the help to become parents, but said there must "be adequate protections for those who enter the surrogacy system."
"We need to make sure bad actors don't ruin it for everyone else," she said.
On Tuesday, officials said the Arcadia Police Department requested assistance from the LA County Sheriff's Department in early September. A Los Angeles FBI spokesperson confirmed the FBI served a search warrant at the home, separate from a search conducted by the sheriff's department.
"We will continue to work together to pursue justice for all 21 children involved in this case," Luna said.
Maria Castellanos, a surrogate who carried two children for Zhang and Xuan, said after learning of their arrest, "I'm mad that everyone involved couldn't stop this so the kids wouldn't go through everything they went through. I'm just mad with the whole process, the whole thing. It's not just them."
"I trusted Silvia," she said.
Josh  Boswell contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Rapid City freshmen experience real-world risks at Freshman Impact
articles.title_zh: Rapid City freshmen experience real-world risks at Freshman Impact
articles.content_orig:
RAPID CITY, S.D. (KOTA) - Rapid City freshmen are getting hands-on lessons in the consequences of risky decisions through the annual Freshman Impact: Caught in the Moment program.
The full-day program is being held Tuesday, Oct. 6, at Central High School, and Wednesday, Oct. 7, at the South Dakota National Guard Armory for Stevens High School students. Nearly 1,000 freshmen are expected to take part.
At Central, students tried navigating a driving course while wearing Fatal Vision goggles that simulate impairment.
“It was like, you know, those kaleidoscopes where you look into them. It’s all spinny triangles,” said student Henry Zimmerman.
The program includes stations on seat belt use, CPR, substance use and online safety. A new station features a state snowplow, teaching students about the truck’s blind spots and the dangers they can pose on the road.
In the afternoon, students see a mock crash response involving first responders, followed by a mock funeral and sentencing hearing.
“We’re trying to do a little bit of mind changing where they make better choices,” said Rick McPherson, director of Freshman Impact.
Organizers say emergency vehicles, equipment, lights and sirens at the schools and armory are part of the planned prevention exercise. Visitors must sign in at the welcome desk.

articles.title_orig: Trump will not reimburse federal government for taxpayer-funded advertisements
articles.title_zh: Trump will not reimburse federal government for taxpayer-funded advertisements
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump said Monday he will no longer use taxpayer money to fund a series of promotional television ads , announcing that he will instead pay for them with funds raised for MAGA, Inc., the pro-Trump super PAC.
“The Radical Left is upset with the fact that I am taking Ads, which I consider to be a positive promotion for our Great U.S.A., and paying for them with U.S.A. money. This is a rather standard thing to do but, rather than doing that, although nothing will make them happy, I have decided to do the Patriotic Ads, among others, and pay for them myself, and with money I raised for MAGA, Inc. MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN!” Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social .
The reversal follows criticism of the administration’s multimillion-dollar television advertising effort, which Republicans and Democrats alike have questioned. The White House has defended the spots as public service announcements.
As of Monday, at least an estimated $10.1 million in taxpayer dollars have been spent on the ads, according to a leading political ad-tracking firm, AdImpact. It is unclear if the administration plans to continue spending the $20 million total that was originally allocated for the effort. Asked about its plans, a White House spokesperson did not respond to the question and only confirmed that Trump is not going to reimburse the government for the money already spent on the ad buys.
As of last week, the administration had created at least 13 campaign-style ads promoting Trump and his policies. Spots that have yet to air include three ads highlighting the US military and operations in Iran and Venezuela, one titled “God Made Trump” and another recapping the UFC fight Trump hosted at the White House.
CNN obtained clips of 12 of the ads , ranging from 15 seconds to three minutes long, two of which have already aired. They appeared in a Dropbox account shared with CNN and run by LMD, the agency awarded the government contract for the ad buys. Each ad ends with the words “Paid for by the U.S. Government” at the bottom of the screen. Another ad, “Final Battle,” which is not in the Dropbox account, has also aired in recent weeks.
While each of the ads has a different theme, many of them include imagery of the president and audio with positive reviews from news reports. They also include patriotic images — including the cap toss at a military graduation, fireworks over Mount Rushmore and military flyovers.
Trump has personally driven the video ads, CNN previously reported , including helping select the imagery and footage, according to a source familiar with the matter. Two Trump advisers said the ads were being produced in-house by the White House video team, part of the communications office responsible for the administration’s public messaging, though at least one was produced by a pro-Trump meme group.
Watchdog groups have said the ads mark a clear violation of appropriations law restricting the use of federal funding for propaganda or partisan communications, but it’s not clear if outside groups have standing to file a lawsuit. Though the ads have received bipartisan criticism, Congress — which groups said had the clearest lane to provide some accountability — did not act to block the ads ahead of the midterms.
This story has been updated with additional reporting.
CNN’s Betsy Klein contributed to this report.

articles.title_zh: Christa Pike is conscious and speaking after failed execution, attorneys say
articles.content_orig:
She was initially on a ventilator after the execution attempt, attorneys said.
Christa Pike is conscious and speaking nearly a week after a botched execution left her critically injured and temporarily on a ventilator, her attorneys said Tuesday.
"Her recovery is medically unprecedented. Her prognosis remains unclear but, at a minimum, we expect a long recovery," her attorneys -- Randy Spivey and Kelly Gleason from the Tennessee Office of the Post Conviction Defender and Stephen Ferrell and Luke Ihnen from Federal Defender Services of Eastern Tennessee -- said in a statement.
Pike, 50, continues to receive medical care after she survived being administered two lethal doses of pentobarbital and was hospitalized following the failed Sept. 30 execution in Nashville, her attorneys said. She has "severe damage" to her arms and remains handcuffed to her bed, her attorneys said.
"We are incredibly grateful to the first responders and the medical team at the hospital who treated Christa like a human and have provided exceptional care to her," her attorneys said. "We also want to thank thousands from all over the world who sent messages offering prayers and support for Christa."
Pike, the lone woman on Tennessee's death row, was sentenced to death after being convicted of the 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. Her attempted execution by lethal injection came after a series of last-minute legal challenges.
Her attorneys said Tuesday they continue to ask Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee to commute her sentence to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole.
The Tennessee Department of Correction confirmed Tuesday that Pike remains hospitalized but said it could not provide details of her medical condition due to federal privacy laws.
Pike's attorneys filed an emergency motion in Davidson County Chancery Court last week seeking an order requiring the Tennessee Department of Correction to preserve all relevant physical, written and electronic evidence related to the execution attempt.
A status conference on the matter has been scheduled for Wednesday.
According to the motion, Pike "could be heard crying, whimpering, and breathing loudly" while being administered two lethal doses of pentobarbital, at one point stating that her arm "feels like it's about to burst open." At least seven needles were used to gain IV access, with one "bent in a 90-degree angle when it was removed," the motion stated.
The motion described pentobarbital, a sedating medication, as being "caustic and highly alkaline" and that it "burns upon contact." Both of Pike's arms were "swollen, burned, and blistered" when she arrived at a Nashville-area hospital, the motion stated.
Pike had raised concerns about a lethal injection in the months prior to her scheduled execution, arguing that her "thrombocytosis, post traumatic stress disorder and small veins 'make it sure or very likely that there is a substantial risk that she will experience unnecessary and superadded pain and suffering, terror, and disgrace,'" the motion stated.
Pike is the first person reported to have survived lethal injection after being given medications, according to the Death Penalty Information Center, whose executive director referred to the failed attempt as "the worst we've ever seen and unlike any other botched execution in the modern era."
In the wake of the botched execution, Gov. Lee ordered a temporary halt to scheduled executions in the state and Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada resigned .
The governor's office said in a statement that it has also appointed former U.S. Attorney Ed Stanton to conduct an independent review of the Tennessee Department of Correction's execution attempt that "will seek to determine whether the protocol was followed and consider whether additional recommendations are necessary to ensure the State's protocol continues to be lawful and effective."
"The State previously retained Stanton in 2022 to conduct an independent review of Tennessee's lethal injection protocol. His work prompted the State and Attorney General's Office to substantially rewrite the protocol before executions resumed," the statement further said.

articles.title_orig: California couple arrested on child abuse charges in horrifying surrogacy probe
articles.title_zh: California couple arrested on child abuse charges in horrifying surrogacy probe
articles.content_orig:
A Southern California couple who had 21 children , most of whom were birthed by different surrogate mothers, lied to the surrogates and then subjected the children to vicious beatings and punishments, authorities said.
Silvia Zhang and Guojun Xuan were arrested Tuesday after authorities served a search warrant at their Arcadia mansion as part of a child abuse investigation. They have been charged with conspiracy to commit child abuse and witness intimidation.
Xuan also faces one felony count of child abuse, one felony count of accessory after the fact and five felony counts of dissuading a witness. Zhang also faces one count of accessory after the fact and four counts of dissuading a witness.
In court Tuesday afternoon, they pleaded not guilty and denied all allegations.
Attorney Mitchell Krems, who represented the couple in court on Tuesday, said in an interview with NBC News that Xuan did not commit child abuse, “didn’t need surrogacy for money” and is being “unfairly scrutinized” because of his Chinese background and unusually large family.
“He’s exercising his civil liberties to be able to have as many children as he wants,” Krems told NBC News. “There’s no law against that.”
He said the size of Xuan’s family is the result of his experience in China and its former one-child policy, replaced in 2021 to allow married couples to have three children, and his desire to have a large family.
“He moved to the United States so he can exercise his liberty to have as many children as he wants,” Krems said.
Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman said Zhang and Xuan’s residence, described by the DA’s office as a mansion in the city of Arcadia, 20 miles northeast of downtown L.A., was the setting for egregious abuse.
“This house could only be described as a house of horrors for these incredibly young children,” Hochman said at a Tuesday news conference.
Authorities began investigating the couple last year after a 2-month-old child was brought to the hospital with head injuries. Hochman, citing a criminal complaint, alleged that a nanny struck the baby in the head on May 4, 2025.
Xuan and Zhang did not seek medical attention until days later, he said, noting that the baby has since recovered.
Krems called what happend to the infant “horrible,” but said the blame lay squarely on the nanny and not Xuan.
“My client fired the nanny after he found out that she was abusing the child,” Krems said.
During the investigation, authorities learned that Xuan and Zhang were running a surrogacy ring out of their home and hired surrogates throughout the country.
Hochman said the couple often lied to the women about why they wanted children or how many children they already had .
“One surrogate in particular … was paid for both a first and second surrogacy,” he said. “She was told initially Zhang was a single mother struggling to conceive when she agreed to act as a surrogate. That was a false statement.”
The woman was paid up to $75,000 per surrogacy, the district attorney said.
The couple failed to tell another woman who was seven months pregnant that they already had 16 children, he said.
“Another surrogate, they said they were seeking the miracle baby, and they paid that surrogate $135,000,” Hochman said.
Over the years, the children were allegedly abused while Xuan and Zhang watched on 32 motion-activated cameras they set up around the home, Hochman said.
He described three rooms the couple called “learning rooms,” where the children would spend hours seated at desks under the supervision of various nannies.
“Each one of these defendants monitored the nannies’ discipline of the children that were happening in the three learning centers,” the district attorney said.
He said during one incident, a nanny had forced a child “to maintain a horse stance” and Xuan could be seen on video laughing.
“In another situation, defendant Xuan entered one of the learning centers while a nanny was striking a child, and instructed the nanny to strike the child harder,” he said.
Hochman alleged that Xuan also beat a child across the child’s bare buttocks and struck the child’s head.
“Defendant Xuan also lifted the child into the air by one arm, while continuing to strike him and repeatedly struck the child’s head from side to side with sufficient force that the child’s body lurched into alternating directions with the blows,” he told reporters.
He said the children were punished, physically abused and beaten “on a daily basis.”
One room in the home did not have cameras. Hochman said the children would be taken into the room and could be heard “screaming from inside.”
The couple is accused of trying to cover up the alleged abuse by instructing the children to lie, according to Hochman. During a meeting after the 2-month-old was taken to the hospital, the couple allegedly told the nannies not to leave visible marks on the children.
“This case is unprecedented,” Hochman said. “It is horrific, and the physical abuse, beating, and punishment that these very young children received is despicable.”
Chunmei Li, the nanny alleged to have been seen on video hitting the 2-month-old baby, was charged in May 2025 with felony child abuse, according to the DA’s office and court records.
The 58-year-old is the subject of an arrest warrant and has not been apprehended, according to records. There is no attorney listed for her in court records, and the L.A. County public defender’s office did not immediately respond Tuesday to an email seeking comment if so.
Krems said Xuan “fired the nanny and the people who are culpable for inappropriate discipline.”
Los Angeles County Sheriff Robert G. Luna said the children were subjected to “horrific abuse.”
All 21 children are now in state custody.
Prosecutors sought $100 million bail per person because of the serious nature of the charges and because authorities said the pair are flight risks.
The judge set bail at $20 million each with home detention and a protective order against visiting their children.
A bail review hearing has been set for Monday.
Minyvonne Burke is a senior breaking news reporter for NBC News.
David Douglas is a supervising producer for NBC News based in Los Angeles.
Dana Griffin is an NBC News correspondent.

articles.title_orig: Jaguar targets young Americans with Type 01 EV – but it’s too long for UK parking spaces
articles.title_zh: Jaguar targets young Americans with Type 01 EV – but it’s too long for UK parking spaces
articles.content_orig:
Latest model is launching in New York to target rich US buyers – and is more than 5.2 metres long and 2 metres wide
It has no rear window, will not fit into a UK parking space and – starting at £130,000 – ($172,000) is aimed squarely at rich tech industry buyers driving the wide open roads of America.
Jaguar’s electric car, the Type 01, was launched in New York on Tuesday night and marks the culmination of a two-year rebrand that has been one of the most scrutinised in automotive history.
Bosses hope the vehicle will appeal to a younger, richer audience than the manufacturer’s previous “shrinking and ageing” customer base of “men in their 50s”, said Rawdon Glover, 58, Jaguar’s managing director.
With an ultra-long bonnet, low roof and muscular design, the Type 01 is a sharp departure from its predecessor, the F-Type. It is also double the F-Type’s starting price of about £62,000.
Buyers are likely to be rich, “urban” and “very design literate, very technology literate”, Glover said. “The person making this purchase will be choosing the car because it’s a bold choice.”
A senior JLR executive close to the Type 01 project put it more bluntly: “It’s the type of car that you park up and everybody stops and says: ‘Fucking hell, what have you just turned up in?’”
The launch comes at a critical juncture for parent company Jaguar Land Rover (JLR), which has grappled with falling sales as cheaper Chinese rivals eat into its UK market share. It is still recovering from a massive cyber-attack last year that cost the economy an estimated £1.9bn.
JLR recently announced 4,000 job cuts in an attempt to save £1.7bn over two years, citing “intense competition and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty”. The Guardian understands Jaguar employees working on the Type 01 programme were offered voluntary redundancy along with the rest of JLR’s non-manufacturing workforce.
The car will go on sale in early 2027, with the first deliveries anticipated in the second half of the year.
“It’s really important that we put Jaguar back on a more solid financial footing,” Glover said. Asked if doubling prices would be effective, he said it was better than “to toil away as we have done for the last two decades in the volume premium space”.
Range Rover also unveiled its first fully electric model in September with a starting price of £154,070 compared with £107,530 for its combustion engine predecessor.
Waning demand in China, a key market for luxury cars, has also hit Jaguar hard. Glover revealed that the Type 01 will not launch in the country for “a couple of years. We’ve decided just to hold off on that.”
However, he added that China would eventually be “an important part of the equation … it’s very difficult for any car manufacturer to exclude the single largest car market in the world”.
after newsletter promotion
PB Balaji, the JLR chief executive, has said the parent company will pivot towards North America and target more sales to millionaires and billionaires to turn its fortunes around.
Glover admitted that while the Type 01’s launch was in New York, it “absolutely” could have been in Silicon Valley instead, reflecting the type of buyer Jaguar is targeting. He recently took a prototype to the offices of Nvidia, the California-based AI company, whose boss, Jensen Huang, had a ride and “loved it”.
The car has no rear window, instead mounting a rear-facing camera where a traditional mirror would be. The car produces more than 1,000 horsepower and Jaguar says it will travel up to 400 miles on a single charge.
It follows a controversial rebrand that started with an ad in late 2024 featuring stern-faced models without a car in sight. The ad prompted a backlash online and was followed by the Type 00 concept car that was unveiled in “Miami pink”, which Donald Trump described it as “woke” while Nigel Farage said Jaguar deserved to go bust.
Glover admitted the backlash “wasn’t always easy” but added: “The reality is we will need to attract a new audience.”
It is just as well: at 2 metres (6ft 5in) wide the Type 01 will hog the British country lanes frequented by Jaguar’s old customer base, while at more than 5.2 metres in length it will not fit in a standard 4.8 metre UK parking space.
“There are long cars out there on the market,” Glover argued, adding that a Land Rover Defender with a wheel on the back is longer than the Type 01, which he claimed had the “turning circle of a Fiat 500” with its all-wheel steering. “It is incredibly manoeuvrable.”
The business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, said: “Jaguar’s new EV is a crucial step in JLR’s plans to invest over £15bn in the UK, and another big vote of confidence in our world-class automotive industry. “This cutting-edge new model being designed, engineered and built in Britain will support thousands of jobs across the West Midlands and North West, and builds on over £1bn of UK automotive investment secured just last month – marking another step forward in our mission to reindustrialise Britain.”

articles.title_orig: From 'woke' ridicule to real car - new electric Jaguar unveiled
articles.title_zh: From 'woke' ridicule to real car - new electric Jaguar unveiled
articles.content_orig:
Two years ago, Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) relaunched Jaguar into a blizzard of controversy. Its bizarre teaser ad was described as "woke" and its "Barbie pink" concept car was ridiculed.
Now, the first of its new models has appeared in public for the first time. The all-electric Type 01, unveiled in New York, represents a radical new direction for the classic brand .
The car itself is an imposing four-door "Grand Tourer", with a long bonnet that deliberately harks back to Jaguar's emblematic 1960s E-Type.
But it marks a gamble for JLR, which has invested billions reinventing Jaguar and is facing mixed reactions over the new car's design and the brand's all-electric strategy.
The new model's electric motors are potent, producing about 1000 horsepower and allowing it to accelerate from 0-62mph in 3.2 seconds. JLR says it has a range, at "sustained highway speed", of up to 320 miles.
The company describes it as the "most technically advanced, powerful and aerodynamic Jaguar ever engineered".
However, it comes at a hefty price tag, with a minimum cost of £130,000 ($172,426). In the US, the Type 01 has a starting price of $130,500.
Under normal circumstances, the launch of a car like this might generate few headlines. But in this case the attention has been much greater, and for good reason.
In 2024 Jaguar unveiled its new identity to the public. The first step was a surreal advert, showing models in a range of bizarre and brightly coloured outfits. There was a new Jaguar logo - but no cars in sight.
Two weeks later, Jaguar's denim-clad design chief Gerry McGovern took to a Miami stage to unveil a pair of radical concept cars , resplendent in Miami Pink and London Blue colour schemes. "Jaguar has no desire to be loved by everybody," he quipped.
The event was meant to herald Jaguar's future as a luxury all-electric marque , but it triggered a furious backlash in the press and on social media.
Critics claimed JLR was betraying its heritage in favour of going "woke". Even the colour chosen for the launch was derided as "Barbie pink", as culture wars erupted around it.
The reception appeared to catch JLR by surprise. The reinvention of Jaguar as a luxury electric brand was part of a wide-ranging strategy set out by the company in early 2023, in which it pledged to invest £15bn in new models and technologies.
At the time, Jaguar itself was struggling. The badge, which was once an intrinsic part of Swinging Sixties British cool, had lost its lustre. Where in the past it had supplied E-Types to Brigitte Bardot and Steve McQueen, it now struggled to sell upmarket saloons and SUVs to middle-ranking corporate executives, who generally preferred Audis and BMWs.
"Jaguar's core demographic, despite the uproar, gave up on the brand years ago, so they effectively had nothing to lose," explains Matthias Schmidt of Schmidt Automotive Research.
The unveiling of the Type 01 on Tuesday was met with mixed reactions, with some on social media criticising the new car.
"Looks like a Cybertruck and a Bentley Continental had an illegitimate child," Facebook user Ken Katch said, referring to the Tesla pick-up, known for its divisive design.
Craig Kinnersley, who runs a luxury car consultancy, wrote on LinkedIn that it is an "unmitigated catastrophe" that looks like a hearse and lacks any "memorable Jaguar flourish".
"We are watching the people running JLR dance on the brand's grave," he added.
"At least it isn't boring," said a Facebook post.
Alistair Weaver from vehicle sales platform Edmunds said Jaguar deserved some credit for the Type 01's looks, despite it being "polarising".
"If Jaguar designed a car that looked like anything else, it would have had no hope," Weaver told the BBC.
But the firm faces an uphill battle in the US, where EVs are becoming less popular ,    he added.
JLR wound down production of its old Jaguar models in 2024 and 2025. The "woke" row, while it possibly made life briefly uncomfortable for the company's leadership, did at least keep the Jaguar name in the public consciousness at a time when it was selling very few cars.
"It brought Jaguar from the back pages to the front pages, given that it was dying in a crowded international market," says Schmidt. "Everyone is now talking about what would have been another boring product."
The GT is expected to be the first of three new electric designs from Jaguar.
Since that event in Miami two years ago, McGovern has left the company, JLR has parted ways with the agency behind the controversial rebranding campaign, and the company also has a new chief executive.
But the future of Jaguar itself still hangs in the balance.
"I think it really is a last throw of the dice," says automotive journalist Steve Fowler. "JLR has struggled to make serious money with Jaguar in the past, and that's what it's all about."
The question now is whether enough buyers can be found willing to pay £130,000 for a relatively distinctive upmarket electric car, in a market where they can also choose models from the likes of Porsche, Mercedes-AMG or even fast-growing Chinese brands such as Denza.
"Forget the controversy, the culture wars and the pink concept car," says Ginny Buckley of the electric car website Electrifying.com.
"What ultimately matters is whether Jaguar has built something extraordinary enough to justify blowing up everything it stood for before."
She believes the car is good enough to silence critics, but admits "the next challenge will be getting people to buy it".
Steve Fowler agrees. "The car is good enough to do it," he says. "Whether the Jaguar brand is good enough remains to be seen."

articles.title_orig: Soybeans left out of U.S.-China trade talks; Minnesota farmer weighs in
articles.title_zh: Soybeans left out of U.S.-China trade talks; Minnesota farmer weighs in
articles.content_orig:
ROCHESTER, Minn. (KTTC) – Soybeans were excluded from the U.S.-China trade talks in late September. The lack of discussion on the crop was not what the American Soybean Association (ASA) hoped for.
“ASA is disappointed U.S. soybeans were not included among the agricultural products receiving additional tariff relief from China,” the organization wrote on its website. “China’s remaining 10% retaliatory duty limits access for private Chinese importers, meaning soybean trade will continue to be handled primarily by China’s state-owned enterprises. Removing the tariff would improve the competitiveness of U.S. soybeans and provide greater opportunity for private Chinese buyers.”
According to ASA, China is committed to 25 million metric tons of U.S. soybeans annually for 2026, 2027 and 2028.
“Any time we talk about trade in China, it’s always big news,” said Darin Johnson, who is the director of the Minnesota Soybean Growers Association. “We were a little bit let down about the lack of discussion about soybeans and trade going into the future.”
Johnson is a fourth-generation Faribault County soybean farmer. He said he was generally happy that the trade talks happened; however, it would have been ideal if the existing tariff on the agricultural product had been cut.
“The 10% tariff remains on, which is unfortunate for us as a US soybean producer,” Johnson said. “It puts us at a competitive disadvantage globally, unfortunately, especially against our biggest competitor: South America.”
KTTC spoke with University of Minnesota McKnight Professor of Applied Economics Carlisle Runge regarding the topic. He said the lack of discussion is damaging for Midwestern soybean producers.
“The Chinese want to maintain the soybean trade as leverage for further negotiations,” Runge said. “By most estimates, the trade in soybeans with China has fallen year on year anywhere from 50% to 75%.”
As a farmer, Johnson said input costs have been the main concern. He said crop prices have been better.
“We’re pretty lucky to be able to have an opportunity to be able to at least start selling some of our commodities, at least above break even at this point,” Johnson said. “Things are starting to look a little bit brighter.”
Minnesota is the third-largest state exporter of soybeans to China. Iowa and Illinois rank first and second.

articles.title_orig: S&P 500, Nasdaq reach record closing highs as focus pivots to earnings
articles.title_zh: S&P 500, Nasdaq reach record closing highs as focus pivots to earnings
articles.content_orig:
The S&P 500 rose to an all-time intraday on Tuesday, touching 7844.52 and surpassing its August 13 intraday peak when it hit 7,830. The benchmark also closed for the first time over 7,800.
The recovery comes after months of oil shocks, rising borrowing costs and the possible start of a Federal Reserve rate hiking cycle.
The record rally comes just a day after the 10-year Treasury yield surpassed 5.3%, reaching levels not seen since 2002. In mid September, the Fed raised its benchmark rate for the first time in over three years and indicated more were to come.
Oil had crossed $100 a barrel in early March for the first time since 2022 as the Iran conflict disrupted energy supplies moving through the Strait of Hormuz. After falling below $70 a barrel, it slingshot back above $100 in early September.
"At the end of the day, oil and bond yields can be correlated, but so is the stock market and profits. And if the profits are there, which they have been, the stock market is going to be resilient, even if the economy is a bit more mixed," Shawn Snyder, economic strategist at Potomac Fund Management, told CNBC.
Unlike prior records this year, this latest run has been narrowly lead by a few stocks tied to the AI hype and deemed unfettered by adverse macroeconomic headwinds.
"When traders take a breather from the noise surrounding them — much of it negative in recent months — and look closer at what's happening in the markets, it becomes clear the U.S. stock market is the best place to park their money compared with other locations. It's hard to argue against the mostly positive risk-reward ratio we've seen over multiple decades," said JJ Kinahan, Cboe Global Markets senior vice president of retail and alternative investments.
The so-called Magnificent 7 namely, Nvidia , Alphabet , Amazon , Apple , Meta , Microsoft and Tesla make up more than 34% of the market cap of the S&P 500 .
"When you consider that much girth among a small handful of stocks, it's apparent how much these stocks' daily movements dictate the direction of the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq, both of which are in record territory again today," Kinahan said.
With tech companies investing heavily in data centers and computing infrastructure demand for chips and equipment has gone up. Earlier this year, Amazon said it expected about $200 billion in capital expenditures across its businesses in 2026, citing opportunities including AI, chips and robotics.
Investor appetite for ambitious technology bets also became evident in June, when SpaceX raised $75 billion in the largest IPO ever and began trading on June 12. The debut became another milestone where investors continued backing growth companies despite higher energy prices and borrowing costs.
Looking ahead, however, Potomac Fund Management's Snyder cautioned that the "weakening" market breadth may last longer if inflation shows no signs of easing, or if there's no clear signal that the Federal Reserve is achieving its mandate. The central bank is slated to release its minutes from the September meeting on Wednesday.
The market "can look relatively calm, but there are still things going on underneath the surface that may not be so calm," Snyder said.
Correction: The 10-year Treasury yield on Monday surpassed 5.3% to reach highs not seen since 2002. An earlier version misstated the year.

articles.title_orig: Bulgaria's leader says drone attack hits 2 commercial vessels, and Ukraine's president blames Russia
articles.title_zh: Bulgaria's leader says drone attack hits 2 commercial vessels, and Ukraine's president blames Russia
articles.content_orig:
Drone attack sinks ship off NATO ally Bulgaria as expert warns Russia is ‘taking things up a notch’.
A commercial ship sank and its crew vanished Tuesday after an apparent coordinated air-and-sea drone attack off NATO member Bulgaria, as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed Russia before warning Moscow was preparing a broader "massive strike."
A second vessel was also heavily damaged and set ablaze inside Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone, with a drone expert warning the dual precision strikes signaled a dangerous escalation and possible "larger invasion posture" by Russia.
"They were likely using the Geran-4 aerial drone to take the vessel out or the Maran surface vehicle to take it out," Cameron Chell, founder of drone manufacturer Draganfly , told Fox News Digital on Tuesday of the first strike.
RUSSIA MAY BE USING HIDDEN 'LUNCHBOX-SIZE' DRONE DEVICES TO COUNTER UKRAINE DEFENSES: EXPERT
The dual attack occurred roughly 70 nautical miles off the eastern Bulgarian coastal town of Byala, according to Reuters, bringing the conflict into the economic zone of a NATO member. (REUTERS/Petko Momchilov TPX IMAGES)
"The reason it wasn't just an air vehicle or an air drone that took this ship out was that the Gerans generally come in at a pretty steep angle when they're on final attack," Chell said.
"There are not really any precision drones that fly closely above the surface, which is where they would have had to hit in order to create an impact that would sink this ship fast enough," he added.
"The nature of this strike suggests there was a combination of an air attack and surface attack," Chell said.
The dual attack occurred roughly 70 nautical miles off the eastern Bulgarian coastal town of Byala, according to Reuters , bringing the conflict into the economic zone of a NATO member.
Zelenskyy said Ukrainian intelligence and security services were working to determine the full circumstances surrounding the attack.
US ALLIES NEED TO SHOOT DOWN RUSSIAN AIRCRAFT TESTING NATO BOUNDARIES, CZECH PRESIDENT WARNS
"Our intelligence and special services are now working to establish all available information about yet another attack in the Black Sea targeting civilian vessels," he wrote on X.
"Our Navy contacted its counterparts in Bulgaria, and it has been established that this was a combined Russian attack using maritime and aerial drones."
Chell suggested the attack’s location and hybrid nature could serve Russia by sowing greater uncertainty across the region.
"We can see the amount of geopolitical chaos that's involved, and this is exactly the type of thing that would benefit Russia in the region," Chell said.
"The hybrid element here is really blurring the lines between traditional military actions," he added, describing the attack as "an expansion of strategy and tactics."
"This is indicative of this larger invasion posture that seems to be unfolding for Russia," Chell said. "And a real desire, what appears to be, for Russia to take things up a notch."
RUSSIA'S SHADOW WAR IS PUTTING EUROPE ON EDGE AS GERMANY CONFRONTS A GROWING THREAT
In this pool photograph distributed by the Russian state agency Sputnik, Russia's President Vladimir Putin attends a meeting with U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner in Moscow on Sept. 5, 2026. (Gavriil GRIGOROV / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)
Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev also confirmed that aerial and maritime drones targeted two commercial vessels in shipping lanes inside Bulgaria’s EEZ , calling the attack a "gross, flagrant violation of international law," according to Reuters.
The sunken vessel, identified by British maritime risk group Vanguard as the cargo ship Alfa Watan, suffered catastrophic structural damage before submerging with an undisclosed cargo and an unknown number of crew members aboard.
A nearby Bulgarian ferry, the Dioscuria, diverted to the scene after witnessing an explosion and receiving distress signals, Reuters reported.
Rescuers found an overturned lifeboat, life rafts and life jackets floating in the debris field.
RUSSIA PREPARING HYBRID ATTACKS ON NATO'S EASTERN FLANK, INTELLIGENCE WARNS

articles.title_orig: Tropical threat brewing in Gulf could impact U.S. as a hurricane this weekend. See maps, possible path.
articles.title_zh: Tropical threat brewing in Gulf could impact U.S. as a hurricane this weekend. See maps, possible path.
articles.content_orig:
With less than two months remaining in the 2026 hurricane season , the potential for a ninth named tropical storm in the Atlantic basin is brewing in the southern Gulf.
Since the Atlantic's season began on June 1, it has only seen eight named storms this year, while El Niño continues to bring a more active season in the Pacific. The season ends Nov. 30.
Tropical Depression Nine formed in the Gulf on Tuesday. As the storm brews over the warmer waters off Mexico, it's expected to become a tropical storm by early Wednesday and a hurricane on Thursday, according to the National Hurricane Center.
If it does become a tropical storm, it would receive the name Isaias, pronounced "ees-ah-EE-ahs."
Forecast models are beginning to come to agreement that the northward motion of this tropical system brings it to the Gulf Coast this weekend.
Regardless of its name or if it develops into a tropical storm, we do know that it will bring moderate to heavy rainfall to the Gulf Coast and into the rest of the Southeast this weekend into early next week.
Some longer-range forecast models also see this moisture eventually reaching the Ohio Valley and Northeast by midweek next week.
Timing, storm intensity and severity of impacts to land with this tropical system are what remain unknown.
While some models have impacts starting Friday evening, others show it beginning later in the weekend.
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis on Tuesday signed an executive order declaring a state of emergency for 25 Florida counties ahead of the storm's arrival. DeSantis said in a statement that the order "ensures communities have the time and resources necessary to prepare for potential severe weather impacts to the Panhandle and Big Bend region of Florida."
While tropical storm and hurricane formation and frequency vary throughout the season, the "I"-named systems tend to be the most retired names within the Atlantic basin.
The most commonly known retired "I"-named storms are Ian (2022), Ida (2021), Irma (2017), and Irene (2011).
When Ike was retired in 2008, Isaias replaced the "I" name on the Atlantic tropical cyclones list, which rotates every six years.

articles.title_orig: France shuts down nearly 900 schools as violent education protests escalate
articles.title_zh: France shuts down nearly 900 schools as violent education protests escalate
articles.content_orig:
France is struggling to contain its biggest student protests in decades. What started as a demonstration in support of striking teachers at a suburban high school to the north of Paris has snowballed into a national crisis.
Hundreds of schools have been forced to close and more than 6,000 people have been taken into police custody over the past few weeks, most of them minors with no previous criminal records. Students, teachers and policemen have been injured. One student in the north-east city of Lens lost his hand after reportedly picking up a grenade and another in Tours, the use of an eye.
Authorities estimate hundreds of thousands of protesters, including students, teachers and delegates from trade unions, took to the streets on Tuesday as protests sweep the country.
In Paris, tear gas filled the air, and trash cans, school desks and chairs were set alight as riot police with shields and batons clashed with some demonstrators.
The original protest at Saint-Exupéry high school in a Parisian suburb on September 21 attracted little attention. Pupils had joined their teachers to protest a lack of staff and resources. When their demands were met and extra staff sent to the school, the strike ended, but by then the match had been lit. According to student leader Manès Nadel, it spread like wildfire.
“It’s an unprecedented number of schools that are now involved,” he said, adding that France’s Education Ministry had been “totally overwhelmed by the crisis.”
Despite their suburban beginnings, the protests are now drawing international attention. US President Donald Trump claimed Tuesday that “what’s happening in France is nothing less than out of control mass migration.”
“This isn’t about schools, this is about Islam wanting to take over a once great country,” Trump posted on Truth Social.
Pupils at lycées in Paris and the surrounding region began blocking entrances, and within days similar scenes were reported across the country, from Lille in the north to Marseille in the south. Images of students setting alight trash cans, manning barricades, assaulting teaching staff and clashing with police led to questions about the police’s response and the far left’s involvement. More than 100 high schools have been damaged since the start of the protest movement.
Critics have accused the police of a heavy-handed response. One policeman was captured on camera using a headlock on a girl in Alençon, a technique now prohibited by law.
The violence and the speed with which the protests have grown have taken many by surprise, but the grievances are long-standing — an overcrowded, ill-equipped and understaffed education system that many students feel is no longer fit for purpose. Videos have circulated for years showing classrooms with too few desks or chairs, or students finding their classes cancelled when an absent teacher is not replaced.
A fertility spike in France in 2010 has led to a rise in the number of high school students now attending schools that have seen years of real-terms funding cuts. Secondary schools now have fewer teachers than in 2008, despite an extra 250,000 students enrolled. In the public sector, 70% of classrooms have more than 30 pupils per class.
Critics say the government’s response has been slow and tin-eared. Initially much of it was focused on the far-left LFI party and its presence at the barricades. The party, led by Jean-Luc Melenchon, who’s expected to do well in the country’s presidential election next spring, has repeatedly defended both the students’ right to protest and his party’s right to be there. There’s also been a lot of focus on the need for a firm police response and the cost of the protest. Damage to schools in the greater Paris region alone is estimated at 7 million euros ($7.84 million).
There was an initial concession over the fees at technological high schools that had been planned for 2027 but this has now been removed from the government’s budget. “The government’s response has been irresponsible and it confirms exactly why the students are angry, because they are never heard,” said Manes. “They are responding only with repression.”
The protesters do now have the government’s full attention, especially after a spike in violence late last week, when the interior minister noted a shift from student protest to urban violence and some 2,000 people were taken into custody in a single day. On Friday, Edouard Geffray, the education minister, met with student leaders. No agreement was reached, however, and the student leaders called for a massive turnout on Tuesday immediately afterward.
France’s interior ministry estimated there were about 256,000 protesters out on the streets nationwide on Tuesday, including 56,000 in Paris. Meanwhile, the Union Syndicale Lycéenne, one of the high school student unions involved in organizing the demonstrations, suggested a much larger turnout of 450,000 people across the country.
More than 400 people were detained in Tuesday’s protests, the ministry said.
Some students have called for fresh demonstrations on Thursday.
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, speaking in the National Assembly on Tuesday, said “extreme violence has reached the gates of our high schools and it must be condemned unequivocally.”
Lecornu said 215 students and 85 education staff have been injured during the unrest, calling it “the highest number of education staff injured in decades.” He rejected accusations that the government had ordered police to repress the protests.
He also said officials must listen to the concerns and demands of students at each school.
“That is why time will be set aside starting this week, from Wednesday, to allow each leadership team to organize a session of internal democracy within its high school,” he wrote on X.
The Education Ministry has launched an online portal where students can share their concerns and ideas for improving their education.
The government’s response is being hampered by the poor state of the public finances. It is trying to pass a 2027 budget that narrows the deficit to around 5 percent of GDP, a feat that can only be achieved by painful belt-tightening. Last week France’s 10-year bond yield briefly topped 5 percent last week, its highest since 2002, as the protests compounded concerns about the country’s fiscal outlook.
The unrest has fired the starting gun on what promises to be a vicious race between the far right and far left for the presidency, with much of the center floundering in the polls. For the far left, the pupils are a natural constituency. For the government, they’re a source of disorder and of spending pressure at the worst possible moment.
Historically, student protests have not gone well for French governments. The student protest of May 1968 turned into the largest strike in French history, in a country that knows a thing or two about strikes. One of its slogans was “be realistic, ask for the impossible.”
The difference now is that the students who’ve taken to the barricades once again don’t feel they are asking for much. In fact, they say they are demanding the bare minimum: an education system that allows them to learn.
CNN’s Saskya Vandoorne, Lucie Lepellec, Kate Irby and Billy Stockwell contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: Germany arrests former intelligence chief in espionage case
articles.title_zh: Germany arrests former intelligence chief in espionage case
articles.content_orig:
If the allegations are confirmed, it would be an espionage case of historic proportions for Germany: August Hanning, former head of the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) , has been arrested , with the federal prosecutor accusing him of espionage, treason and attempted treason.
August Hanning , now 80, headed the BND from 1998 to 2005. But even before then, he had enjoyed a meteoric rise within the security apparatus. After leaving the BND, he served as state secretary in the Federal Interior Ministry, then moved into the private sector and worked as a security consultant.
According to the federal prosecutor's office , his informant was his former chief-of-staff, named in the statement only as Manfred D.*, who went on to hold this position under Hanning's successors from March 2012 to March 2026. D. thus had access to a great deal of classified information.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Manfred D. is alleged to have passed on nearly 2,000 BND documents — some of them highly sensitive — to Hanning over the course of several years in exchange for money. Hanning is then said to have used the information in his private consultancy business.
The most serious allegation is that Hanning is said to have maintained close contact with an employee of a foreign intelligence service for years and to have leaked classified information to him. It is not known which country was involved, but reports say it is not Russia.
Investigators also mention an analysis that Hanning is said to have prepared for an employee of another foreign intelligence service. However, it is not certain whether the analysis ever reached that person.
The classified information also concerned the routine meetings of the heads of German security agencies at the chancellery. Topics included, among other things, the Iranian nuclear program and analyses of the Russian armed forces.
Since intelligence from foreign partner agencies is also said to have been shared in this context, this could also undermine their trust in the German BND and lead to difficulties in future intelligence cooperation with Germany.
Hanning came under scrutiny in an entirely different context
"A good agent is one who doesn't draw attention to himself," Hanning was once quoted as saying. When he finally drew attention to himself, it was in an entirely different context.
In September 2025, the Hamburg state police searched Hanning's home and offices in connection with the famous case of the kidnapping involving Christina Block , heiress to the steakhouse restaurant chain Block House. State prosecutors in Hamburg accused her of having ordered the kidnapping of her two youngest children in late 2023 due to a custody dispute.
A little over a year before the operation to bring the children back, there is said to have already been a failed kidnapping attempt. At the time, there were suspicions that Hanning was involved, which he denies.
But during a search in 2025, investigators found an electronic storage device containing top-secret BND documents. The police handed the documents over to the federal prosecutor's office, which launched a covert investigation against Hanning and Manfred D. in May 2026. The most recent documents found so far are said to date from June 2022.
Throughout its history, the BND has seen a number of espionage cases, some of them spectacular. In the 1960s, Heinz Felfe headed the "Counterintelligence: Soviet Union" division while simultaneously working for the Soviet secret service, the KGB.
In 2014, a BND employee was exposed as a spy for the US CIA. There is also an ongoing trial against a BND agent accused of betraying secrets to Russia's FSB in September and October 2022 — that is, after the start of the war in Ukraine. Yet never before has a former official of August Hanning's stature been at the center of suspicion of espionage.
"The BND launched extensive internal investigations early on and without delay, which corroborated the suspicions," said current BND President Martin Jäger. "For the BND and for me, there can be no compromises when it comes to internal security."
However, there was some fierce criticism from the political sphere. Günter Krings of the conservative governing party, the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), told the Rheinische Post newspaper: "The mere suspicion that a former BND chief is selling secrets is damaging to trust in our security agencies."
Konstantin von Notz of the environmentalist Green Party and deputy chair of the parliamentary committee that oversees the intelligence services said: "These are serious and grave allegations that have been leveled against August Hanning." Speaking on behalf of his party, he called for greater scrutiny of lobbying activities by former top officials and those with the highest security clearances. "These are clearly also a gateway for hostile intelligence services," von Notz said. The federal government must put an immediate stop to these "illegitimate practices."
Clara Bünger, domestic policy spokesperson for the socialist Left Party group in the Bundestag , went even further: "The investigations against former BND chief Hanning show once again: The intelligence services themselves are a security risk."
This article was originally written in German.
*Editor's note: DW follows the German press code, which stresses the importance of protecting the privacy of suspected criminals or victims and urges us to refrain from revealing full names in such cases.
