articles.title_orig: David Ellison backs CNN’s Trump lawsuit, pledges editorial independence
articles.title_zh: David Ellison backs CNN’s Trump lawsuit, pledges editorial independence
articles.content_orig:
CNN’s new owner, David Ellison, says he supports CNN’s legal action against the Trump administration over White House access, and will not interfere in the news organization’s coverage.
“We believe in editorial independence, and we will never interfere,” Ellison said, reiterating the reassurances he made while seeking to buy Warner Bros. Discovery earlier this year.
The merger between Warner and Paramount took effect on Tuesday morning, and Ellison held an employee town hall to introduce the newly combined company, named Skydance.
Later in the day, he fielded questions from reporters at a press conference in Los Angeles.
When asked how Skydance will win over people who opposed the merger, Ellison said, “We’re going to make sure that CNN and CBS News are completely editorially independent. We’re going to build a streaming service that can compete with anybody. And I think that when we actually follow through on all of those promises, I believe it will rebuild trust.”
At both the press conference and town hall, Ellison, the CEO of Skydance, laid out his vision for investing in films, shows and new technology.
David Ellison has built a Hollywood giant in Skydance. Now he wants to make it a tech company
“For the first time,” he told employees, “we have the studios, the franchises, the libraries, the talent and scale all under one roof to compete with anyone in the world.”
While Ellison didn’t name names, he meant media giants like Google, Netflix, and Disney.
CNN anchor Anderson Cooper interviewed Ellison at the town hall and asked directly about CNN employees’ concerns about Skydance’s ownership.
In response, Ellison said, “I believe deeply in journalism,” and went on to call the work done by CBS News and CNN “a vital part of our democracy.”
While speaking about the need for fact-based news, Ellison said, “You go back to what President Obama said during the pandemic. He said a republic that can’t agree on the same set of facts can’t function, and I think he was 100% right about that.”
In the news space, “we want to actually help scale and transition the business digitally,” Ellison said.
He emphasized the importance of growing CNN’s digital operations and reaching new audiences worldwide, citing Skydance’s estimate that the combined company reaches more than 200 million streaming subscribers.
The newly formed company, he said, “can create an even bigger platform for the best journalism in the world.”
The Ellison family’s ties to President Donald Trump had fueled concerns among CNN employees about the network’s independence.
Last fall, Trump described Ellison and his father, the billionaire Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, as “friends of mine” and “big supporters of mine.” Last December, Trump said “it’s imperative that CNN be sold” to new owners.
Asked about the merger on Tuesday afternoon, Trump said, “It’s going to be a great company. They’re terrific people, and it’s going to be a great company.”
At the Skydance town hall, Cooper asked a follow-up question about CNN, MS NOW and Politico’s First Amendment lawsuit over Trump’s recent attempt to ban the three news outlets from the White House.
Cooper asked, “Do you stand with CNN and our effort to completely restore access to covering President Trump?”
“Of course,” Ellison said.
The next hearing in the legal case is slated for Thursday morning.
Both CNN chairman and editor-in-chief Mark Thompson and CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss attended the town hall. The two news operations are operating separately for now.
At the press conference, Ellison praised both news leaders, saying, “We’re thrilled, obviously, with Mark. We’re thrilled with Bari.”
When a reporter asked about Ellison’s relationship with Trump, he answered, “We have a good relationship with this administration. I also had a really good relationship with President Biden. I have a good relationship with Senator Tim Scott, and I have a good relationship with Governor Gavin Newsom. I think it is important to talk to everybody, on both sides of the aisle.”
Mark Thompson to remain CNN chairman as Ellisons take control of Warner Bros. Discovery
“We want to speak to everybody,” Ellison added. “We do not want to politicize the company.” Seemingly referring back to his previous meetings with Trump, Ellison said, “We were in a transaction review process. But with that said, we are now turning that page.”
At the town hall, Cooper asked about the likelihood of a tie-up between CBS and CNN in the future: “If Paramount and Warner Brothers are now cousins, and CBS News and CNN are cousins, when does somebody start to ask them to share organs?”
“It’s day one,” Ellison said.
He said he intends to bring the relevant business leaders “into the decision-making” now that the deal has taken effect.
Generally speaking, companies will start making integration decisions “within usually 120 days,” Ellison said, “but I think it’s foolish to try to say I’m going to show up with every single answer today.”

articles.title_orig: McDonald’s sued over AI tool that recommends prices to US franchisees
articles.title_zh: McDonald’s sued over AI tool that recommends prices to US franchisees
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
McDonald's is facing a federal lawsuit that alleges its AI -enhanced pricing tool violates antitrust laws because it shares nonpublic data with franchisees who might be competing in the same market.
The lawsuit, which was filed Friday in Illinois, said McDonald's pricing tool uses artificial intelligence to collect data that competing franchises wouldn't normally share, like store-level sales. The Chicago-based burger giant has said it makes the tool available to U.S. franchisees to help them set prices at their individual restaurants.
The lawsuit also blames the pricing system for raising McDonald's U.S. prices.
"McDonald's has built and for years deployed its own information-sharing pricing platform, which draws on data from its millions of daily transactions to set menu prices across thousands of U.S. restaurants," the lawsuit states. "The result is algorithmic price-fixing aimed at customers who are already stretched thin."
McDonald's said Tuesday that the lawsuit is "filled with inaccuracies" and it would vigorously defend itself.
"AI does not set menu prices at McDonald's restaurants – McDonald's franchisees do," the company said in a statement. "Optional tools are available to franchisees to help them make the best decisions for their businesses and customers, but these tools do not automate, coordinate or fix pricing in any way."
The lawsuit was filed on behalf of a consumer, Michael Thomas, of DeKalb, Illinois. According to the lawsuit, Thomas frequently visits McDonald's and orders a Quarter Pounder with cheese, french fries and a Coke. The lawsuit said Thomas noticed price differences between McDonald's stores near his home.
McDonald's said it has used an AI-enhanced pricing tool for more than a decade. The program determines the optimal price for menu items based on a store's sales, location and other factors, including competitors' prices.
McDonald's said that long before adopting the AI-enhanced tool, it collected data and recommended prices to its franchisees, who own and operate 95% of McDonald's 14,000 U.S. stores.
"All we do is provide the context of what's going on," a McDonald's spokesman told The Associated Press. "We don't have any way to affect the menu pricing in a restaurant."
But the lawsuit said McDonald's has "significant leverage over its franchisees" and can pressure them to follow its pricing recommendations.
The Associated Press left a message Tuesday with the National Owners Association, which represents McDonald's franchisees.
McDonald's has been experimenting with various value strategies in the U.S. and other markets for several years as it tries to win back lower-income consumers, whose visits to fast-food chains have dropped.
But franchisees don't always follow its guidance. During a conference call with investors in August, McDonald's Chairman and CEO Chris Kempczinski said only 60% of its U.S. restaurants were offering McDonald's proposed menu of 10 items for under $3.
"As you know, in our system, that's not something that we just flip the switch on," Kempczinski said. "It requires conversations with franchisees."
The lawsuit asks the judge to certify the case as a class action and to require McDonald's to pay damages to the class. It also seeks to prevent McDonald's from enforcing agreements that restrict competition.

articles.title_orig: Ravens’ Marlon Humphrey, Tyler Loop to join Trump at Sparrows Point
articles.title_zh: Ravens’ Marlon Humphrey, Tyler Loop to join Trump at Sparrows Point
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump visited Maryland on Tuesday to announce a project that's expected to support 14,000 jobs and become the state's largest job creator in over a decade.
The president toured Tradepoint Atlantic with Anduril Industries, a defense technology firm in Sparrows Point, and announced that the former Bethlehem Steel site will be turned into a 2-million-square-foot shipyard to build components for Virginia-class attack submarines.
According to a media briefing, the components include torpedo tubes, sterns and bow sections, and will be built at the Sparrows Point site.
Maryland Gov. Wes Moore said this will be the largest private investment in the state in more than a decade.
"With this facility, thousands of Marylanders will have new pathways to work, wages, and wealth through advanced training and high-skilled maritime manufacturing jobs," said Moore. "We thank Anduril for choosing Maryland, and we're ready to build the future of the aerospace and defense economy together."
The facility is expected to support 14,000 jobs, including the creation of 3,100 permanent jobs. Over a decade, Arsenal-2, the name of the new industrial base, will become the state's largest job creator.
"For generations, this site shaped America's steel and shipbuilding legacy, including its critical role during World War II, when workers here built the vessels that helped defend our nation," Baltimore County Executive Kathy Klausmeier said in a statement.
The $3.7 billion private capital investment will become the largest single private investment in the state.
Happening right now, @realDonaldTrump has taken the stage in Sparrows Point to officially announce @anduriltech ’s new shipyard to help create the next generation of submarines for the @USNavy ! @wbaltv11 pic.twitter.com/EhDT4ohBt2
"With Arsenal-2, Anduril will return large-scale shipbuilding to a site that can once again define American naval power. This facility will make Baltimore County a critical part of America's submarine industrial base, adding the production capacity that the Navy needs to meet its Virginia-class requirements," said Brian Schimpf, Anduril cofounder and CEO.
Under the agreement, the state and Baltimore County will match up to 13% of the anticipated investment through existing economic incentive programs and new appropriations.
The state would also support the construction of a workforce training facility near Tradepoint Atlantic.

articles.title_orig: China Refiners Flock to Iraqi Crude
articles.title_zh: China Refiners Flock to Iraqi Crude
articles.content_orig:
China’s independent refiners are turning to Iraqi crude after a US blockade choked supplies from top source Iran, while competition from state-owned rivals priced most of them out of Russian barrels.
Private processors, including smaller ‘teapot’ refiners in Shandong province, have bought Iraq’s Basrah Heavy and Basrah Medium grades for November delivery at premiums of as much as $18 a barrel to ICE Brent, according to traders familiar with the matter. The purchases point to a rush for prompt supplies rather than a strong recovery in Chinese oil demand .
At least 50 tankers, mostly carrying Iranian crude, are bottled up along the nation’s coast as a US blockade seeks to pressure Tehran into ending the seven-month war on terms favorable to Washington. At the same time, state-owned Chinese refiners are taking most of the available Russian crude, driving up costs for independent processors.
Inventories at some Shandong teapots could run out as early as the end of this month, forcing refiners to compete for a shrinking pool of alternatives just as Beijing issued fresh crude-import quotas, said Muyu Xu, senior crude analyst at Kpler. “To avoid shutting down or significantly cutting run rates, refiners need to secure alternative supplies as soon as possible.”
The supply squeeze has pushed some processors toward sulfur-rich Basrah crude, which they typically avoid in favor of cheaper Iranian barrels and diesel-rich ESPO from Russia’s Far East.
Improving Middle Eastern flows , as Gulf producers move more oil through the Strait of Hormuz, are also making Iraqi crude increasingly accessible. Producers in the region are deepening discounts to defend market share after Saudi Aramco cut the price of its flagship grade for Asian buyers.
Meanwhile, Russian barrels remain expensive, with ESPO commanding a premium of almost $30 a barrel above Brent, the traders said, asking not to be identified as the negotiations are private.
“Teapots are very price sensitive,” Kpler’s Muyu Xu said, adding that Basrah is now cheaper than Russia’s ESPO, making those barrels increasingly attractive to private refiners.
Buyers of Iraqi crude include both private processors in China’s Shandong province and some large independent refiners, according to the traders. Iraqi barrels are typically marketed by trading houses such as Vitol Group, Trafigura Group and Mercuria Energy Group, as well as TotalEnergies SE.
Iran was a major crude supplier to China’s independent refiners before the blockade, with imports exceeding 1 million barrels a day prior to the war. Private processors were the main buyers, attracted by steep discounts on sanctioned barrels that bolstered refining margins.

Germany’s former foreign intelligence chief has been detained on suspicion of passing state secrets to a foreign intelligence service, the country’s federal prosecutor’s office has said.
Prosecutors allege August Hanning, whose tenure at the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) ended in 2005, paid for access to classified documents from a former aide at the BND. It is claimed Hanning used them to prepare an analysis which he intended to sell on to a foreign intelligence service as part of his consulting activities.
He is “strongly suspected of treasonous espionage, spying out state secrets, attempted treason and espionage”, the federal prosecutor’s office said in a statement.
Prosecutors did not identify which foreign intelligence service he was allegedly preparing the analysis for, and it ⁠was not immediately clear whether it reached its intended recipient.
According to German newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung the case does not ⁠involve Russia.
Hanning, 80, was arrested in Bad Tölz-Wolfratshausen in southern Germany on Tuesday. The former aide, ‌identified only as Manfred D, was also arrested on Tuesday in Steinfurt in western Germany.
Manfred D is charged with aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage.
Prosecutors said they are also searching the suspects’ premises in these locations and in Berlin.
From the spring of 2010 until July 2022, Manfred D continuously obtained valuable information for Hanning from the BND in exchange for payment, said the prosecutor’s statement.
He allegedly provided him with nearly 2,000 documents, many of them classified and intended solely for internal use within the BND and senior-level intelligence ‌briefings at the chancellery.
According to the statement, Hanning was in close contact with a member of another state intelligence service, and he supplied this individual with political information over several years, which was partly based on material he had received from Manfred D.
Hanning was president of the BND from December 1998 to November 2005. Manfred D served as his chief of staff at that time, and later served as chief of staff for several subsequent BND presidents from 2012 until 2026.
“In his role, he had access to confidential information,” the prosecutor's office said.
The German newspaper Bild said that the investigation was launched after the discovery of an alleged leak of intelligence reports intended for the chancellery.
The arrests came after a separate investigation into allegations that Hanning abducted Hamburg businesswoman Christina Block’s children from her ex-husband in Denmark in January 2024 in a custody battle that had been going on for several years.
The current investigation stems from evidence found during a search of Hanning’s residence in connection with that case, the federal prosecutor’s office stated.
Both of the accused will be brought before the investigating judge of the Federal Court of Justice on Tuesday and Wednesday.
German opposition lawmaker Konstantin von Notz voiced his shock about the allegations against Hanning and called for a quick investigation.
“This is a hard-hitting and deeply troubling story,” said von Notz, a member of the Greens party and also the German parliament committee overseeing the intelligence services.
“We expect a swift and thorough investigation into the egregious allegations levelled against former BND chief Hanning,” von Notz told Spiegel Online.

articles.content_orig:
It’s day three of the 2026 World Championships here in Baku.
International Judo Federation President Mr Marius Vizer and CEO of CBH Bank, Mr Simon Benhamou, signed a sponsorship agreement.
And an MOU was signed between the IJF General Treasurer Dr Naser Al Tamimi and the International Police Sports Union Secretary General, Gonzalo Londono
As the National Gymnastics Arena filled, fans were treated to the chance to meet some of their judo heroes, before settling in for another fantastic day of competition.
Current World Champion, Eteri LIPARTELIANI made it to the final once again at -57Kg.
LIPARTELIANI provided some of the highlight throws of the day!
Trying to take the title was Japan’s Akari OMORI . Throughout the prelims, OMORI showed how dangerous she can be in standing and groundwork. Her toughest fight came from teammate Momo TAMAOKI. A huge victory on the road to the final.
In a tense final that entered golden score, OMORI showed her dominance on the ground, successfully turning over and holding down the current world champion to take the title.
CBH Bank CEO Mr Simon BENHAMOU, Awarded the medals.
At -73KG, TANAKA Ryuga had a tough draw, but after successfully defeating the category’s top seed, a waza-ari score in the semi-final put him in contention for gold.
World number 3, Makhmadbek MAKHMADBEKOV of the UAE already has a World bronze, and today he was hoping to finally take the top spot. A fantastic display of skill and power in the preliminaries made that look possible.
The final was another close battle, with just a single score enough to take the victory.
It was TANAKA who struck the winning blow, an incredible driving ouchi-gari, taking down MAKHMADBEKOV for a yuko score. Two new world champions for Japan, crowned on Day 3!
General Treasurer of the International Judo Federation Mr Naser AL TAMIMI awarded the medals.
We’ll see you tomorrow for Day 4.

articles.title_orig: Cornell Faculty Senate introduces no-confidence resolution over handling of alleged 2024 sexual assault
articles.title_zh: Cornell Faculty Senate introduces no-confidence resolution over handling of alleged 2024 sexual assault
articles.content_orig:
ITHACA, N.Y. — Cornell University faculty members introduced a resolution calling for a no-confidence vote in the university administration’s handling of the alleged 2024 sexual assault at a fraternity house.
The resolution was submitted to the University Faculty Committee on Monday evening, according to a copy obtained by NBC News.
“That the Faculty Senate has no confidence in the ability of the central administration to effectively address the ongoing crisis of sexual assault at Cornell University,” says the resolution, which is less than half a page.
The measure is expected to be considered by the Faculty Senate, which meets Oct. 14, Faculty Senate member Paul Ortiz said in a statement.
Ortiz said in an interview: “My primary job as an educator is to make sure my students are studying and learning in a safe environment. If they don’t feel safe, they can’t learn, they can’t study, they can’t thrive, they can’t grow as individual human beings.”
Ortiz added that there is a “climate of fear among women students.” He emphasized that the Senate’s goal is to force “systemic change” rather than advocate to have one or two people, such as university President Michael Kotlikoff, step down.
You get “rid of one person, and then you bring a new person into a dysfunctional environment,” Ortiz said.
“A lot of the students would like the president to step down, but we decided not to have that in the resolution,” he added.
In a statement accompanying the resolution, the faculty sponsors said “numerous Cornell colleagues” had approached them demanding action, while students had told faculty members they were “upset [and] fearful for their personal safety” and wanted the Ivy League school to address sexual assault on campus.
Cornell alumni had also contacted faculty members and shared “their own traumatic stories as students,” the statement said.
Cornell declined to comment.
The proposed no-confidence resolution escalates the pressure on Cornell and its administration following national scrutiny over how the case was handled. Last month, a former student identified as Jane Doe sued the university and seven current and former students in connection with her allegation of sexual assault.
She alleges that multiple fraternity members sexually assaulted her in October 2024 while she was impaired by alcohol, ketamine and marijuana.
The woman’s allegations have made national headlines for days, and they prompted protests on campus following widespread criticism that the university and local officials did not do enough to investigate them.
Anne Marie Elizabeth Brady, a Faculty Senate member and research director for the university’s Industrial and Labor Relations Workers Institute, said the resolution came together “quickly” in recent days.
“If I was a woman on Cornell’s campus, I’d run in the other direction,” she said. “Because I’m not sure Cornell is there to protect the students the way they should be.”
Brady said Cornell’s decision to discipline the seven men accused of wrongdoing instead of passing the case on to outside law enforcement “feels like a cover-up to me.”
“If I’m a betting woman, I suspect they didn’t do that because they wanted to keep it secret,” she said. “They wanted to manage the story.”
If the Faculty Senate passes the resolution, Brady said, it will then prompt a series of discussions between faculty members and Cornell’s leadership for policies about sexual assault.
Similar action was taken last year following years of campus protests of the war in Gaza. Brady said those recommendations have largely been ignored.
“If the administration came out and said: ‘You know what? We screwed up, we did A, B and C wrong. We failed this student, we failed all our students through this process and these are the concrete ways and steps we are going to take to change,’” she said, “if they did that? That goes so far.”
Adam Reiss and Maggie Vespa reported from Ithaca and Matt Lavietes from New York City.
Adam Reiss is a reporter and producer for NBC and MSNBC.
I’m a reporter on NBC News’ breaking news team, covering crime, extreme weather, pop culture and more. I recently covered Hurricane Milton, which devastated the Tampa, Florida, metropolitan area, and the student-led protests at Columbia University.

articles.title_orig: Much of the world sees tragedy in Gaza. Many Israelis, scarred by Oct. 7, see only a threat
articles.title_zh: Much of the world sees tragedy in Gaza. Many Israelis, scarred by Oct. 7, see only a threat
articles.content_orig:
Israeli communities shattered by Hamas massacres are torn between rebuilding their lives and remembering lost friends and relatives
K eith Siegel spent many of his long hours in Hamas captivity in Gaza etching everything that happened after 7 October 2023 into his memory. For 484 days, he recited to himself every place he was held, the dates he was moved and every attack or humiliation he endured or witnessed.
He aimed to store intelligence that could help Israeli forces free other hostages if he was released, to keep track of time as the days slid by and be able to tell his family what happened to him. Now his body is free, but he cannot loosen those memories.
“I’m living a kind of dual life,” he said in an interview in Tel Aviv. “I’m here for some of the time, and I’m in Gaza some of time. It’s very challenging to convey in words what it was like.”
Siegel and his wife, Aviva, were among 251 people taken captive to Gaza on the deadliest day in Israel’s history, when Hamas militants broke across the border to launch a wave of attacks on kibbutzim, border towns, military bases and music festivals.
Israel’s security forces were caught by surprise, and by the time they regained control of the area, 1,209 people had been killed, the majority of them civilians, including 36 children, according to records kept by the Israeli newspaper Haaretz.
The cemetery at Nir Oz contains two lines of fresh headstones, marking lives that all ended on that same date. A shared plot for a family of five – a mother, father and their three young children – has been made into a garden with space left for their still-living grandparents.
Caretaker Shlomo Margalit, who will soon turn 89, points to the graves of three of his oldest friends, founding members of the kibbutz who came to Nir Oz from Haifa with him in the 1950s.
“This is my life project, as well as my home,” Margalit said, explaining why he has come back to a place of such loss. He is waiting for a new house but, for now, staying in the former home of Gadi Moses, 82, who survived 482 days as a hostage.
The graves he tends are a silent testament to the brutality of the attacks and the scale of the state’s failure, which in Nir Oz was staggering, even on a day of terrible failures.
A five-person volunteer defence force held Hamas at bay for at least two hours, Margalit said. When they had all been shot, the kibbutz was taken over and sacked, homes burned, families slaughtered and kidnapped.
Then, before the first Israeli soldier arrived, the Hamas forces, other Palestinian gunmen and civilian looters all left. Nir Oz had been forgotten by the army and ripped apart without the military firing a single shot to defend it.
In total, 47 people were killed and 76 taken to Gaza, including Shiri Bibas , her 10-month-old baby Kfir and four-year-old Ariel, who were killed in Gaza. The dead and hostages represented more than a quarter of the small community.
Revisiting that terrible day, and the trauma that followed, is painful and exhausting for Margalit, but he still accepts interviews for a simple reason. “I want people to know what really happened here,” the 89-year-old said.
The third anniversary of the 7 October attacks falls a few weeks before national elections, and much of the country is caught up in a furious debate about responsibility for the deadliest day in Israel’s history and the conduct of the war that followed.
Survivors and bereaved relatives are avoiding the political fray, still grappling with the trauma and the struggle to rebuild something like normality.
In Nir Oz, there is a terrible, almost irreconcilable struggle between re-establishing the kibbutz as a living community, and preserving physical testimony of the attack.
The cemetery echoes with the sound of construction and families have already moved into several rows of new houses near the kibbutz entrance.
But on the other side of the compound, paths still lead between blackened ruins and memorials to the dead. Some bereaved survivors want the homes of loved ones preserved this way as permanent monuments to mark their loss.
“There are families that can’t [bear to] live here, but want a memorial place to come to visit,” Margalit said. “On the other hand, can you build a new kibbutz where children grow up running around between burnt houses?”
He is on the remembrance committee and, two years on, they are struggling to reach a decision on this impossible choice. “Is there right or wrong here? No,” he said. “We are dealing with that, trying to find an answer.”
One compromise might be a memorial garden on the border of the kibbutz. For now, there are plaques with the stories of families attacked on that day and a memorial house to remember the dead and kidnapped.
When the kibbutz took a collective decision to return and rebuild, Margalit and his wife, Hanna, knew they wanted to join. His only concession to the trauma was asking for a new home that did not face Gaza.
“I’ve found myself building this place for the second time,” he said. “I know when I’m gone, I will have done something with my life. I took part in putting this spot on the map.”
The Siegels, who lived in the nearby kibbutz of Kfar Aza, also among the worst hit, have decided not to return as they focus on mental and physical recovery. Aviva was 62 when she was kidnapped. Keith was 64.
“ What happened to me in Gaza, what happened with Keith in Gaza, it’s there all the time,” said Aviva.
“I understand that it’s going to be a process of healing. There’s always things that remind me, and if I don’t remember, then he reminds me. If I’m cooking lunch or making a cup of tea and I turn around and see Keith with tears in his eyes, because he just read something or let himself feel.”
The days approaching the anniversary have been particularly difficult, she said. Last year, at this time, she was still campaigning for the release of other hostages, her own emotions held at bay by the urgency of that campaign.
For a time, she tried to deal with the trauma by telling herself, over and over again “I must feel lucky,” simply because she had made it back alive.
Now she has allowed herself to feel again, and as 7 October approached, she has realised how raw the wounds still are. “Getting ready [for the anniversary] has been very very painful,” she said. “The last couple of weeks all I want to do is cry. Now I’m feeling things I didn’t feel before.”
“When I hear my grandson say he is afraid of being kidnapped in the middle of the night, it breaks my heart.”
She has written a book, Survived to Tell , about the ordeal, which she describes as therapy and an act of celebration. She wrote so her grandchildren could read about what she and Keith endured, for other hostages who couldn’t tell their own stories and to inspire a broader audience in Israel and beyond.
After the exhausting campaign to get Keith and other hostages home, she said she had struggled to concentrate on the election. Keith’s political focus is an independent inquiry into 7 October to prevent other families suffering as his has.
He said: “There needs to be an investigation to understand how this happened, in order to do everything possible that it won’t happen again. So many people were killed, injured, traumatised.”
Benjamin Netanyahu, the prime minister, has fiercely opposed an independent state commission of inquiry. Critics say he is afraid it would expose his own failings.
In the immediate aftermath of the attacks, few people inside or outside Israel expected him to stay in power long, particularly as the country’s coalition governments have rarely served out their full terms.
Netanyahu had for years championed a foreign and security policy based on the premise that Hamas was “contained” in Gaza, behind unbreachable layers of fortifications.
The security officials who were in command that day have all stepped down yet, three years on, Netanyahu is still in power, having deflected all demands for his resignation.
Yaakov Godo, a bereaved fath

The USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service has released revised versions of the New World Screwworm Response Playbook and associated supplemental documents. These updates reflect the feedback and priorities discussed during the first Quarterly NWS Playbook Review meeting held on Sept. 9.
Stakeholder input is essential to ensure that the playbook and supplemental materials remain clear, practical and responsive to operational needs across states, industry and federal partners.
New World Screwworm Response Playbook
Clarifies when zone sizing may be adjusted, such as due to habitat or host factors (Section 2).
New World Screwworm National Continuity of Business Standardized Animal Movement Guidance
Allows states to authorize movement requirement activities to be performed on other premises types, including temporary aggregation points, such as when activities cannot be completed at the origin premises.
Clarifies that animals moving to slaughter from the infested zone may have the 72-hour clock reset following reinspection by an authorized inspector.

Ready Reference Guide - Establishing and Releasing NWS Zones and Areas
Clarifies when zone sizing may be adjusted.
Adds a new section outlining criteria for releasing infested zones.

articles.title_orig: U.K. Security Adviser Traveled to Israel Ahead of Consulate Closure
articles.title_zh: U.K. Security Adviser Traveled to Israel Ahead of Consulate Closure
articles.content_orig:
London, United Kingdom – The deadline Israel imposed on the United Kingdom to close its East Jerusalem consulate is fast approaching.
Thursday marks 30 days since Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar’s order, a retaliatory move against the UK’s wave of sanctions targeting illegal Israeli settlements.
“It’s not the act of a friend or ally,” Sir Vincent Fean, former British consul general to Jerusalem, told Al Jazeera. “The British Consulate General has every right to be in Jerusalem, in East Jerusalem, part of the state of Palestine.”
From 2010 until 2014, Fean held the post as the de facto ambassador to occupied Palestinian territory. He is now a trustee of the Britain Palestine Project, advocating for equal rights for Palestinians and Israelis.
“In international law, for [the UK], and for the vast majority of the world, Israel does not have the right to interfere with the diplomatic relations between the state of Palestine and the state of the United Kingdom. It is doing so by closing our office, and that is unlawful,” he said, adding that he is “particularly concerned” for the consulate’s 50 or so Palestinian staff.
UK-Israel ties have reached a nadir. On Monday, reports claimed that the UK could expel 27 Israeli diplomats if the consulate closure goes ahead.
British National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell has reportedly held talks with Israeli officials in a visit that was not disclosed by the UK government, but an agreement to keep the consulate open was not reached.
Israel’s response was furious following the UK’s import ban on goods from illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank, as well as an overall change of tone. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has, for instance, lamented Israel’s “ethnic cleansing” against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
Miliband expected Israel to retaliate, but said the UK had “weighed the costs and benefits of acting”.
In addition to the consulate closure order, Israel expelled the UK from the Washington-led coordination centre for post-war Gaza and barred 11 lawmakers from entering Israel, including former Labour Party leader Jeremy Corbyn and Zarah Sultana.
“It is illegal and unlawful for Israel to act in this way,” Fean told Al Jazeera. “There’s been a reset in UK foreign policy since [Prime Minister Andy] Burnham and Miliband came in.”
Israel’s hostile actions towards the UK “will not be forgiven or forgotten anytime soon”, he added.
In a brief by the Britain Palestine Project that was endorsed by former UK Attorney General Dominic Grieve KC and shared with Al Jazeera, the threatened closure is described as “an unlawful assertion of sovereignty over occupied Palestinian territory”.
“The Israeli announcement usurps the rights of the State of Palestine,” it reads.
Resolution 478 was adopted by the United Nations Security Council – of which the UK is a permanent member – in 1980, resolving that Israel’s attempts to alter the status of Jerusalem are “null and void”.
In 2016, Resolution 2334 reiterated this, “condemning all measures aimed at altering the demographic composition, character and status of the Palestinian Territory occupied since 1967, including East Jerusalem”.
The UK formally recognised the State of Palestine in September of 2025 .
If the UK resists Israel’s orders, there are various logistical challenges Israel could feasibly impose on the consulate and the diplomats within it.
“The practicality is that the Consulate General depends on Israeli electricity [and] water. So there are means by which Israel could force the expulsion, the closure, of the Consulate General,” Fean told Al Jazeera. “I don’t know what’s going to happen, but this Israeli government has broken many laws,” he said when asked if Israel may use electricity or water cut-offs as a means to expel British diplomats.
While reiterating that the UK’s East Jerusalem consulate should remain open despite orders, Fean said that “if that proves to be made impossible by force of the Israeli government, then there are alternatives.”
Foreign embassies in Ramallah could be an alternate route to manage consulate affairs, he said.
The consulate acts as the channel of communications between the UK and the Palestinian government and manages consular affairs for British nationals in the region, including pilgrims to the West Bank.
“Yet again, Israel is taking it out on the Palestinians for something that somebody else has done,” said Fean. “The impunity of Israel needs to be challenged. The fact that this Israeli government seems to see itself as above the law needs to be challenged.”
Human rights advocates have urged the UK to resist Israel’s orders.
“Such a retaliatory step from Israel suggests that any further measures taken by the UK could trigger further responses,” said Zena Agha, deputy director of the British Palestinian Committee. “But that should not deter the UK from meeting its obligations under international law – nor pursuing measures towards accountability for Israel’s genocide and occupation.”
Shamiul Joarder, director of Friends of al-Aqsa, reiterated the illegality of Israel’s actions and told Al Jazeera, “If Britain accepts this order, it risks allowing Israel to dictate the terms of Britain’s diplomatic presence in occupied East Jerusalem. That would set a deeply concerning precedent.”
The Foreign, Commonwealth, and Development Office (FCDO) did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment on Israel’s orders to close the British Consulate, nor on the UK’s intended response.

articles.title_orig: FSU brings entrepreneurship educators from around the world to Tallahassee for training
articles.title_zh: FSU brings entrepreneurship educators from around the world to Tallahassee for training
articles.content_orig:
Home / News / FSU Global / FSU brings entrepreneurship educators from around the world to Tallahassee for training
Florida State University welcomed entrepreneu r ship educators and leaders from around the world to Tallahassee last month for the 26th Experiential Classroom , an intensive professional development program designed to strengthen entrepreneurship educat ion .
Hosted by FSU’s Jim Moran College of Entrepreneurship , this year’s program took place Sept. 17-19 and brought together participants from six countries, 21 U.S. states and Puerto Rico, representing 58 institutions and organizations. International participants came to Tallahassee from Canada, Ecuador, the Dominican Republic, Armenia and India.
The Experiential Classroom is housed at FSU and offered in partnership with the University of Notre Dame , the University of Tampa and the University of Florida . It was founded in 1999 by Michael Morris, a faculty member of the McKenna Center for Human Development and Global Business in the Keough School of Global Affairs at the University of Notre Dame.
The program has become a leading professional development experience for faculty, doctoral students, program directors and others seeking to strengthen how they teach entrepreneurship.
“The reach of this year’s Experiential Classroom speaks to the global leadership role Florida State’s Jim Moran College plays in entrepreneurship education,” said Michael Brady, interim dean of the Jim Moran College of Entrepreneurship. “We want FSU to be a destination not only for students who want to study entrepreneurship, but also for educators from around the world who want to become better at teaching it.”
While most participants came from colleges and universities, the cohort also included representatives from a high school and school district, as well as and community organizations such as the Chicago Urban League, mHUB and the Chicago Community Trust.
Unlike a traditional academic conference, the Experiential Classroom operates as an immersive teaching clinic. Participants learn alongside experienced entrepreneurship educators through classroom demonstrations, interactive sessions and hands-on exercises they can adapt to their own classrooms and entrepreneurship programs.
“The Experiential Classroom is about learning how to teach entrepreneurship by experiencing great entrepreneurship education,” said Susana Santos, Jim Moran Associate Professor of Entrepreneurship and co-director of the program. “Bringing together educators with different disciplinary, institutional and cultural perspectives creates an incredible learning environment. Participants leave with practical approaches they can immediately put to work and a global network of colleagues to rely on long after the clinic ends.”
The Experiential Classroom is part of FSU’s broader work to strengthen entrepreneurship education in the United States and abroad.
In 2025, Santos and Eric Liguori, Jim Moran Professor and associate dean for research and external relations in the college, traveled to Armenia with Vilma Fuentes, a visiting associate in research at FSU’s Learning Systems Institute , to train more than 30 faculty and administrators at the Armenian State University of Economics (ASUE) on contemporary approaches to entrepreneurship education.
The training was part of a U.S. Department of State-funded partnership designed to strengthen STEM and social entrepreneurship education and educational ties between the United States and Armenia. Liguori also regularly leads entrepreneurship educator development programs at universities across the United States, extending FSU’s expertise in experiential entrepreneurship education to faculty and institutions beyond the university’s campuses.
FSU’s work to advance entrepreneurship education internationally is also expanding through a strategic partnership with Universal AI University in Mumbai, India. Through the partnership, FSU faculty are working with their counterparts in India to help integrate entrepreneurship education into the university’s curriculum, bringing together FSU’s expertise in entrepreneurship education with Universal AI University’s focus on artificial intelligence and emerging technology.
FSU’s role as a hub for entrepreneurship education will be on display again Oct. 15-17, when the Jim Moran College of Entrepreneurship hosts the 2026 Global Consortium of Entrepreneurship Centers Annual Conference, bringing hundreds of university entrepreneurship leaders, educators and ecosystem builders from around the world to Tallahassee.
For more information about conference registration and sponsorship opportunities, visit the conference’s webpage . To learn more about the Jim Moran College of Entrepreneurship, visit jimmorancollege.fsu.edu .
To learn more about FSU’s global footprint, visit global.fsu.edu .

articles.title_orig: TOP FIVE STORYLINES: Sheldon Haudenschild’s Homecoming Sends World of Outlaws to Three Ohio Ovals
articles.title_zh: TOP FIVE STORYLINES: Sheldon Haudenschild’s Homecoming Sends World of Outlaws to Three Ohio Ovals
articles.content_orig:
October 6, 2026 at 3:04 pm
Sheldon Haudenschild cares deeply for his Ohio roots and continuing the state’s rich Sprint Car racing tradition.
The Wooster, OH native’s passion will be on display this weekend as he’s bringing the World of Outlaws NOS Energy Drink Sprint Car Series to his home state for a tripleheader at three different racetracks. Sheldon Haudenschild ’s NOS Energy Drink Buckeye Brawl Weekend sets the stage for a big trip to the “Buckeye State.” All three races will dish out $18,000 to the winner, a nod to Haudenschild’s car number with KCP Racing.
The brawl begins at Findlay, OH’s Millstream Speedway on Thursday, Oct. 8. The tour returned last year for the first time since 1994 and is back for a second consecutive season.
Round two takes The Greatest Show on Dirt to Mansfield Speedway on Friday, Oct. 9. Matt Tift and his team revived the historic track and are ready to welcome the World of Outlaws for the first time in 45 years.
The “Buckeye State” showcase is finalized on Saturday, Oct. 10, at Hartford, OH’s Sharon Speedway as the World of Outlaws makes its 16th stop at the northeast Ohio facility.
Let’s look at the top stories to watch this week:
The KCP Racing pit area will be busy all three nights this week.
Sheldon Haudenschild has amassed one of the most passionate followings in the sport, and it’s felt nowhere more than when he comes home. The Ohio fans watched his dad Jac Haudenschild ride the Haud Line to 72 World of Outlaws victories and many more accolades, and they’ve watched Sheldon follow in his footsteps in carving out his own legacy. He’s up to 55 career wins with nine of them coming this year, his first campaign with the KCP team.
Haudenschild would love nothing more than to add to that total this week. He’s won before at Millstream, topping a 2016 All Star Circuit of Champions (ASCoC) visit. Friday will mark his debut at Mansfield. He bagged a Sharon trophy with ASCoC in 2015 at the Lou Blaney Memorial . In World of Outlaws competition, he’s finished on the podium in four of his six tries. Sheldon Haudenschild has had this weekend circled on his calendar all year (Tyler Carr Photo)
David Gravel is closing in on history.
A rough stretch in California for the two-time opened the door for Michael “Buddy” Kofoid ’s championship hopes, but Gravel did his best to shut it as the scene shifted east. A win and a fourth at Williams Grove Speedway ’s National Open upped his point lead to 142 with just 10 races remaining. If he can hold on, he’ll join Steve Kinser, Donny Schatz , and Brad Sweet as only the fourth driver to ever claim three consecutive titles.
Don’t expect Gravel to stumble on Thursday as he enters Millstream as the defending winner at the Findlay, OH track. The Watertown, CT will make his first Mansfield laps the next night. He and Big Game Motorsports have been stellar at Sharon with a 2.8 average finish in six tries, highlighted by a 2024 triumph.
A trio of California-born World of Outlaws competitors ( Buddy Kofoid , Carson Macedo , and Cole Macedo ) consider Ohio a home away from home and look forward to any swing through the state. All three are united in the Linder family providing them a place to stay as they expanded their racing careers eastward.
Kofoid sits second in the standings heading to Ohio during his third tour with Roth Motorsports. His Millstream debut a year ago resulted in a runner-up finish. The time with the Linders led him to making one prior appearance at Mansfield, a fourth-place effort in 2019. He’s made four Sharon appearances, peaking at second last year.
Carson Macedo resides fourth in points, a manageable 32 markers back of Sheldon Haudenschild for third. His three trips to Millstream yielded a best finish of ninth last year in the Jason Johnson Racing No. 41. The Lemoore, CA native owns more Mansfield experience than most of his fellow World of Outlaws drivers with five starts leading to three podiums, including a 2018 Sprint Car World Championship prelim score. None of Macedo’s 10 Sharon Feature starts have resulted in a win, but he’s been on the podium on four occasions.
Cole Macedo’s sophomore World of Outlaws season sees him sitting eighth in the standings, which would mark a two-spot improvement over his rookie campaign if he can stay there. He took the TwoC Racing ride from 14th to seventh at Millstream last year. He’ll get his first look at Mansfield Saturday. Last year in his seventh Sharon appearance, the 26-year-old started on the pole and finished a solid sixth.
And speaking of Cole Macedo , he leads the most hotly contested battle in the points. Spots eight through 12 are separated by only 120 markers. The point fund and exclusivity bonus pay $70,000 more to finish eighth over 12th, so the five drivers in this fight will be scratching and clawing for every point they can get.
Behind Macedo, next in line is Spencer Bayston as his first year with Stenhouse Jr./Marshall Racing winds down. He won the season opener and has piled up 32 top 10s. He trails Macedo by 62.
Then it’s leading Kevin Gobrecht Rookie of the Year presented by Five Star Bodies contender Emerson Axsom 16 markers back of Bayston. Axsom and the Klaasmeyer/Petry Motorsports team have found some speed over the last couple months with 13 top 10s in 17 races, highlighted by Axsom’s first World of Outlaws win at Huset’s Speedway.
Only two points behind Axsom is Bill Balog . The “North Pole Nightmare” has dealt with several cases of bad luck recently, but his speed over that time suggests it wouldn’t be a surprise at all if the No. 17B breaks through into Victory Lane soon.
Rounding out the group is Series sophomore Chris Windom with 40 markers separating him from Balog. He got his first career victory in August at I-55 and picked up a pair of podiums last month in the Sides Motorsports No. 7S. Cole Macedo leads a hotly contested battle for eighth in the standings into Ohio (Tyler Carr Photo)
The World of Outlaws will have a group of talented “Buckeyes” ready to brawl this week with hopes of battling the best of the best for wins on the sport’s biggest stage.
Dale Blaney may only show up at Sharon, but he’s likely to make the most of that appearance. Last year he wheeled his brother Dave’s No. 10 to an extremely popular win at their home track, becoming the oldest victor in Series history at 61 years old.
Bradner, OH’s Nate Dussel has won at both Mansfield and Sharon this year. He’s topped a pair of FAST races at Mansfield and beat the ASCoC at Sharon in August.
Bellevue, OH’s Cap Henry is always one to watch when the World of Outlaws roll into his local region. He’s won nine 410 Sprint Car races in 2026, including Mansfield’s season opener in May.
These three will be joined by plenty more local gassers looking to impress under the bright lights.

articles.title_orig: Toyota shuts down rumors claiming that it’s ‘slashing prices’ in China
articles.title_zh: Toyota shuts down rumors claiming that it’s ‘slashing prices’ in China
articles.content_orig:
Toyota’s joint venture, FAW Toyota, issued a statement denying reports that it’s “slashing prices” in China and may exit the market entirely.
Toyota sells vehicles in China through two joint ventures: FAW Toyota and GAC Toyota. The long-standing joint ventures produce and sell Toyota models, including the Corolla, RAV4, and Avalon, as well as new electric vehicles like the bZ3 and bZ5.
Last week, on September 28, GAC Group announced plans to acquire a 50% stake in FAW Toyota. The plans include issuing new A-shares priced at 5.75 yuan per share.
Under the agreement, GAC said that FAW Group would become its second-largest shareholder, but exact details would be finalized following an audit and once the valuation work was complete.
FAW Toyota was established in 2000 as a joint venture between FAW Group and Toyota, with each holding a 50% share. It was initially called Tianjin FAW Toyota Motor Co until 2003, when it adopted the name FAW Toyota.
Once the agreement is finalized, GAC Group would take FAW’s 50% stake, while Toyota would retain the other 50%. GAC said the deal would not change the controller.
The move was widely viewed as part of Toyota’s efforts to revamp slumping brand sales in China and streamline operations.
Since the announcement, several reports have claimed that FAW Toyota plans to exit the market completely and is slashing prices to sell down inventory.
FAW Toyota issued a statement on Monday night, refuting the false claims. The company said:
In response to false statements circulating on certain online platforms —such as claims that “FAW Toyota may completely exit the market” and “Toyota is slashing prices”—our company reserves the right to pursue legal action.
The joint venture added that “the production, sales, and iterative development plans for all models are progressing smoothly as scheduled.”
Looking ahead, FAW Toyota will leverage the Group’s broader resources and technology for upcoming vehicles.
Toyota’s sales in China fell by 22.8% in August, marking the seventh straight month of lower sales due to weak demand for gas and hybrid models amid soaring fuel prices.

articles.title_orig: Julie Jones makes history with silver at the World Archery 3D Championships
articles.title_zh: Julie Jones makes history with silver at the World Archery 3D Championships
articles.content_orig:
YANKTON, S.D. – Julie Jones won silver at the World Archery 3D Championships, and in doing so created history by becoming the first USA woman to win an individual medal at the event, which began in 2003.
Jones was making only her second-ever appearance at the World Archery 3D Championships. She was part of the women’s team including Jayme Buchanan, Katherine Li and Madison Ritter to claim bronze at the 2024 World 3D Championships in Mokrice, Slovenia. Two years on and she did even better.
“It's a little surreal, I'll be honest,” began Julie Jones on hearing she had made history. “I love 3D. That is my passion aside from hunting. I guess if you ask me how I felt about it, I'm glad that I could bring it back for the U.S. team. But it really isn't a short answer. It goes a lot further than that.
"This whole time that I've been shooting, I've had an incredible team of people behind me from the very beginning. They have encouraged, they've pushed, they've believed in me when I had doubts about my own abilities. Without them, none of none of this would have been possible.
“I know that I don't have to prove anything to them but bringing this silver medal home, it's a testament to the training and the coaching that that I've received, that this medal belongs to all of these people, not just to me.”
Jones was seeded seventh after qualification before moving through the bracket with wins over teammate Mandy Boggs, Olga Timofeeva (RUS) and Martina Blahusova (CZE). The U.S. archer from Texas settled for silver after defeat in the gold medal match to fifth seed Judith Wenzl (GER).
“I had 100 percent confidence in the training and the coaching that I'd received," explained Jones. "I knew that if I applied all of the mental work, all of the physical work, as well as the actual shooting, I was reasonably confident that I could be in the top 10. That really wasn't a doubt in my mind.
"I knew that if I ran my process and executed well, that there was a good chance I would be in the top five, if not the top three. So that part of it was not necessarily a surprise to me.
“I've had some health challenges along the way and so day two was not a good day for me physically. And it was a struggle just to make it through the round. So that kind of threw a spanner into it.
“But I'm glad that it worked out as well as it did. I shoot very well under pressure. And I knew that if I could make it into those head-to-head eliminations, that I could work. Even though I had dropped points on day two, I knew that I could work myself back up to a to a better position.”
Julie Jones was also part of the bronze medal-winning traditional mixed team alongside Cody Hasson. Hasson, a double gold medalist at last year’s Pan American Field Championships, finished sixth in the individual men’s event.
Jones added, “I am tickled to death that Cody and I ended up with the bronze medal. He is a really, really strong shooter. I may be mistaken, but I don't think he's ever medaled before (at World 3D), and just to see the excitement and the absolute joy on his and our coach Shiloh's (Butts) face, when we realized that we had won that last round, that was a great feeling.”
For Jones, this was a family affair, with husband Daniel having also made the team. For Daniel, it was not only his World 3D Championship debut but also his first major event outside of local competition. A first major event for Daniel and the first U.S. woman to win an individual medal at the World 3D Championships for Julie. A case of keeping up with the Joneses!
“I'm just a normal person,” continued Julie. “I'm a mom. I have kids. I'm self-employed. I don't have a big, fancy facility, but, you know, I go out and I'm passionate about 3D archery.”
This success comes just a few weeks before a significant birthday for Julie on November 1. She said with a smile, “Just a month before, to achieve this, I couldn’t ask for anything more. This is year 50 for me. I have my 50th birthday coming up. And winning individual silver is pretty much the best present that I could imagine.”
Matt Hudson and Ava Jones combined to take silver in the barebow mixed team. Seeded at number two, the pair defeated Austria (150-136) and Denmark (152-141) before defeat to Russia (144-123). Ava Jones, making her World Archery 3D Championships debut, came in fourth in barebow women.
Other top 10 individual finishes came for Kim Timberlake (4th in longbow women), Joella Bates (8th in longbow women) and Lee Wilkins (10th in longbow men). Timberlake’s march to the bronze medal match included a 96-66 quarterfinals win over third seed Paula Virmasalo (FIN).

articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
New York has recorded 108 measles cases so far this year, most since mid-July.
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul declared a state disaster emergency on Monday as neighboring Pennsylvania battles its largest measles outbreak in three decades.
As of Oct. 3, New York has recorded 108 measles cases so far this year, 92 of those since mid-July across 18 rural counties where communities are under-immunized, according to Hochul's order.
"After reviewing the latest data on measles cases in New York State, I am declaring a state disaster emergency to strengthen our ongoing efforts to confront this disease," Hochul said in a statement . "No one should get seriously ill or die from a vaccine-preventable disease."
It marks the first time a state has issued an emergency order since measles cases began rising last year. At least 95% of measles cases in the U.S. have been among people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown.
The order allows registered nurses to order the collection and testing of specimens for suspected measles cases.
Early symptoms include cough, runny nose, fever as high as 104 Fahrenheit and red, watery eyes, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
Two to three days after symptoms start, patients may develop Koplik spots, which are tiny white spots that may appear inside the mouth on the inner cheek.
Three to five days after symptoms start, patients may experience a rash, first appearing on the face at the hairline before moving downwards to the neck, chest, stomach, arms, legs and feet. Fever may spike even higher than 104 F when the rash appears, the CDC says.
The order, in effect until Nov. 4, allows pharmacists in New York to vaccinate ⁠children as young as age 2 with the MMR shot. It also expands who can administer MMR vaccines to include emergency medical technicians-paramedics, advanced EMS and midwives.
Additionally, it suspends a previous requirement that health care professionals who administer vaccines to those aged 19 and older receive consent before reporting vaccination to New York City or New York State immunizations registries. All MMR vaccinations of children and adults must be reported within 72 hours.
"Department staff are working closely with local health departments and regional partners to track and contain the current measles outbreak," Dr. James McDonald, commissioner for the New York State Department, said in a statement. "The measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine is the best protection -- protecting nearly all people against disease who receive the recommended doses."
The state said it has administered more than 1,000 MMR shots in rural areas since July.
Meanwhile, Pennsylvania health officials are now reporting more than 1,000 measles cases. Nearly 200 people have been hospitalized and the state has reported five measles-associated deaths, which is the most any state has reported in over 30 years.
This outbreak follows a trend of growing outbreaks in the U.S. over the last two years.
Earlier this year, South Carolina reported the end to a measles outbreak of 997 cases. Last year, Texas reported an outbreak of 762 cases.
Nationally, nearly 4,000 cases have been confirmed this year in the U.S., with infections reported in almost every state, according to the CDC . It's the highest number of illnesses from measles since 1991.
The CDC currently recommends that people receive two doses of the MMR vaccine, the first at ages 12 to 15 months and the second between 4 and 6 years old. One dose is 93% effective in preventing measles infection, and two doses are 97% effective, the CDC says.
Infants aged 6 to 11 months living in or traveling to high-risk outbreak areas may receive an early third dose of the MMR vaccine.
However, CDC data shows vaccination rates have been lagging in recent years. During the 2025-26 school year, 92.4% of kindergartners received the MMR vaccine, according to data. This is lower than the 95.2% seen in the 2019-20 school year, prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.
School vaccine exemptions also reached a record high last school year. Recent CDC data showed that vaccine exemptions for kindergarteners increased to 4.2% during the 2025-26 school year. This is up from 3.6% compared to the previous school year and 2.2% during the 2020-21 school year.

NEW JERSEY - If you’re looking to add a spooky adventure to your Halloween season, skip the haunted houses and fill up the gas tank instead.
While places like Salem and Sleepy Hollow get all the October glory, the ultimate paranormal thrill ride may actually be hiding in the woods of New Jersey.
Clinton Road in West Milford, Passaic County, in New Jersey is officially the most haunted road in America, and the entire world, according to a 2026 data study by SIXT that analyzed millions of global Google and TikTok searches to rank supernatural hotspots,
Racking up over 1 million Google searches and massive viral interest in the past year alone, this notorious road is a paranormal magnet that leaves even the bravest drivers locking their doors.

articles.title_zh: Newsom calls for 25th Amendment after Trump’s remarks on California
articles.content_orig:
Musician Jack White has fired back at Donald Trump following the president’s remarks made that Iran could “take out Los Angeles” and “San Diego” while speaking about the international conflict on Monday at a rally in Nebraska.
“Hey republicans and conservatives that live in L.A. and San Diego; how do you feel about your Fuhrer recommending that the cities you live in get attacked? Click the video I reposted and watch for yourself,” White shared on Instagram Tuesday. “Listen to the cult members CLAPPING and cheering for this. Let me take a wild guess: it was a joke, owning the libs, insert cult rhetoric here, etc. The allegiance these people have to this corrupt felon is so laughable and ignorant.”
He continued: “That’s right, a U.S. ‘President’ that recommended that two major cities in our country be bombed because they don’t give total allegiance to his ego. Imagine any other President or elected official in history saying this. False flag incoming anyone? Just wait till next month when he begins enacting illegal measures to not allow democracy at the polls to prevail when the right lose badly in the mid term elections. I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again: The Worst American of All Time. #TWAAT ”
While onstage, Trump said that raising prices, due to the war, were a “small price to pay for keeping the world safe – keeping our country safe”. “They can take out a city,” Trump continued. “Let them take out Los Angeles. Let them take out San Diego.”
White has long opposed Trump and has blasted the president many times before. In Aug. 2025, the “White Stripes” vocalist took to social media to call him a danger “not just to America but the entire world and that’s not an exaggeration,” and in Feb., mocked Trump’s appearance and track record of international conflict, writing, “Behold the leader of the ‘Board of Peace.’ For the next war announcement donny, may I suggest having your feet up on the Resolute desk while eating a Big Mac in a velvet track suit?”
Gov. Gavin Newsom also spoke out after Trump’s comments, sharing several posts on X . “He is deranged and dangerous,” Newsom wrote in one post. “An American president is talking about Los Angeles and San Diego being ‘taken out.’ Where the hell is Congress? This is dangerous. The time to stand up is NOW,” he wrote in another.
See White’s full post here.

articles.title_zh: Flu season could kick off ‘incredibly’ early — what scientists are watching

A variant of the H1N1 influenza virus is dominating flu season in the Northern Hemisphere so far this year. Shown here are H1N1 influenza virus particles (yellow) releasing from an infected lung cell (green). Credit: Science Photo Library
Data show that flu season in the Northern Hemisphere might be off to an early start — prompting a rethink about when people should get their annual vaccines against the influenza virus . The percentage of positive tests for influenza is unusually high for this time of the year in places such as the United Kingdom and on the West Coast of the United States (see ‘Surprising start’). In Japan, outbreaks in August and early September forced some schools to close just as they were starting back up after the summer break.
“It would be an incredibly early season” for the United States if the cases researchers are seeing on the West Coast continue to rise at their current rate, says Scott Hensley, a virologist at the University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia.
The influenza subtype responsible for most of the US cases so far is H1N1, in a flip from last year, when H3N2 dominated. And sequencing data from these early cases point to an emerging mutation in H1N1 that is causing concern among specialists.
Source: Adapted from US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention data
These findings come from a relatively small number of positive tests compared with those available during peak flu season, so it’s too soon to predict the overall trajectory of the outbreak, researchers say. “An early start doesn’t necessarily mean a more severe season,” says James Hay, an epidemiologist at the University of Oxford, UK. Still, “there is something afoot”, wrote epidemiologist Caitlin Rivers in her newsletter, ‘Force of Infection’, on 27 September .
It’s enough to make Rivers, who is a researcher at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore, Maryland, reconsider her personal protection strategy. In a typical year, when flu season peaks in December and January in the United States, she would wait until mid-to-late October for a shot, to get the best protection. Now, she’s thinking about getting a jab as soon as possible.
Seasonal flu is usually caused by some combination of three viruses: two subtypes of influenza A — H3N2 and H1N1 — and influenza B. Because influenza viruses genetically mutate over time and people’s immunity alters as they get vaccines and infections, which of the three viruses emerges as dominant changes for each flu season. US data showed that, during the week ending on 26 September, H1N1 accounted for 96% of positive cases for which subtyping was performed. H3N2 accounted for almost 4% of cases, and influenza B wasn’t detected.
That’s in contrast to last year, when a new variant of H3N2, called subclade K, emerged. It became globally dominant because it had many mutations that made people more vulnerable to it.
Will the mRNA flu shot work better than a regular seasonal one? What the science says
Will the mRNA flu shot work better than a regular seasonal one? What the science says
This year, the H1N1 mutation that is worrying researchers is G155E. Alex Greninger, a virologist at the University of Washington in Seattle, says that his laboratory detected G155E in 13 of 17 H1N1 samples taken from people in whom the genetic sequences were complete enough to identify specific mutations. The samples had come from hospitals and clinics in Seattle over the past few months.
This mutation had already been flagged in an analysis led by Jesse Bloom, a virologist at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center in Seattle, which was posted on the preprint server bioRxiv last month, ahead of peer review 1 .
Bloom and his colleagues tested how well antibodies in blood samples from 260 people in Australia and the United States were able to recognize and block infection from 148 influenza A viruses circulating by mid-2026. “We saw that a number of strains which have the G155E mutation are, in some cases, less well recognized by pre-existing human antibodies,” Bloom says. Antibodies in serum from teenagers and young adults were especially inept at recognizing this variant, probably because many in these groups haven’t been exposed to H1N1 viruses with similar characteristics before .

articles.title_orig: Idaho sets new Guinness World Record for largest serving of French fries
articles.title_zh: Idaho sets new Guinness World Record for largest serving of French fries
articles.content_orig:
Live updates all day, breaking news as it happens and weather every 10 minutes
Idaho is now home to a new Guinness World Records title after a team served up more than 1,400 pounds of french fries in Boise.
Click here for updates on this story
SOUTHEAST BOISE, Idaho ( KIVI ) -- Idaho is now home to a new Guinness World Records title after the Idaho Potato Commission and Spud Daddy served up more than 1,400 pounds of French fries Friday night.
The team was attempting to beat the previous record for the largest serving of French fries, which stood at 1,452.85 pounds and was set in India in 2018.
“Idaho should have that record,” Thomas Watson with Spud Daddy said. “Idaho doesn’t have that record, and it’s our mission to bring the record home.”
The attempt took plenty of preparation and a large group of volunteers.
Watson said about 50 to 60 people helped cut and flash-freeze the potatoes before they were loaded into a refrigerated truck and eventually fried for the final attempt.
“It’s been awesome just to see it,” Watson said.
About 1,700 pounds of raw Idaho potatoes went into the effort.
After the fries were cooked and weighed, the final total came in at 1,474 pounds — more than 20 pounds above the previous record.
That made Idaho the new Guinness World Records holder for the largest serving of French fries.
The record attempt was part of Potato Days at the Idaho Botanical Garden, a family-friendly event celebrating Idaho's potato industry and the farmers, packers, distributors and retailers behind it.
The event also featured the Big Idaho Potato Truck, live music, lawn games and plenty of potato-based food, including fries, tots, mashed potatoes, loaded baked potatoes and potato soup.
After the record was officially set, Watson said he was ready to finally relax.
“I’m ready to take a nap,” Watson said. “I’m going to be so excited that this thing we have been thinking about is now done. We can go to sleep. We can get some food. We can eat some French fries.”
